at samarbejde.explanation: "At samarbejde" means "to work together", built from sam (together) and arbejde (work): Vi samarbejder om projektet (We are cooperating on the project).

sentence.da: Vi skal **samarbejde** for at løse opgaven.
sentence.en: We have to work together to solve the task.

at samle.explanation: "At samle" means "to gather" or "to collect": Læreren samler børnene (The teacher gathers the children). For a hobby, add på: Jeg samler på frimærker (I collect stamps). It can also mean to put together: Jeg samler en reol (I am putting together a bookcase).

sentence.da: Min bror vil **samle** på gamle mønter.
sentence.en: My brother wants to collect old coins.

at samle på.explanation: "At samle på" means "to collect" as a hobby: Jeg samler på mønter (I collect coins). Without på, at samle means "to gather" or "to pick up": Hun samler blomster (She picks flowers).

sentence.da: Min søn vil **samle på** frimærker.
sentence.en: My son wants to collect stamps.

at sammenligne.explanation: "At sammenligne" means "to compare" and is used with med (with): Jeg sammenligner prisen med prisen i går (I compare the price with yesterday's price). It is built from sammen (together) and ligne (to look like).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sammenligne** priserne i to butikker.
sentence.en: I want to compare the prices in two stores.

at savne.explanation: "At savne" means "to miss" someone or something that is not here: Jeg savner min familie (I miss my family). For missing a bus, Danes say Jeg nåede ikke bussen (I did not catch the bus).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **savne** min familie meget.
sentence.en: I will miss my family a lot.

at scanne.explanation: "At scanne" means "to scan", to copy a paper or a code into a device: Jeg scanner kvitteringen (I scan the receipt). You can also scan a code with your phone.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **scanne** brevet og sende det.
sentence.en: I want to scan the letter and send it.

at score.explanation: "At score" means "to score" a goal or points in sports. It is borrowed from English and is used the same way: Vi scorer i anden halvleg (We score in the second half).

sentence.da: Han vil **score** et mål i kampen.
sentence.en: He wants to score a goal in the match.

at scrolle.explanation: "At scrolle" means "to scroll", to move up or down a page on a screen: Jeg scroller ned for at se mere (I scroll down to see more).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **scrolle** i timevis på min telefon.
sentence.en: I can scroll for hours on my phone.

at se.explanation: "At se" means "to see", and also "to watch": Jeg ser en film (I am watching a film). Jeg kan se, hvad du mener means "I can see what you mean". Vi ses! means "See you!". At kigge (to look) is for looking on purpose: Kig her! (Look here!).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **se** dit hus fra her.
sentence.en: I can see your house from here.

at se efter.explanation: "At se efter" means "to look for" and "to check": Jeg ser efter bussen (I am looking out for the bus). It also means checking: Se efter, om døren er låst (Check whether the door is locked).

sentence.da: Kan du **se efter** mine nøgler?
sentence.en: Can you look for my keys?

at se frem til.explanation: "At se frem til" means "to look forward to": Jeg ser frem til weekenden (I look forward to the weekend). It is common in letters: Jeg ser frem til at høre fra dig (I look forward to hearing from you).

sentence.da: Børnene kan **se frem til** en lang sommerferie.
sentence.en: The children can look forward to a long summer break.

at se på.explanation: "At se på" means "to look at": Jeg ser på billedet (I am looking at the picture). Do not mix it up with at se (to see) or at lede efter (to look for): Jeg leder efter min nøgle (I am looking for my key).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **se på** billedet.
sentence.en: I want to look at the picture.

at se tilbage.explanation: "At se tilbage" means "to look back", with your eyes or in your memory. Han så tilbage over skulderen (He looked back over his shoulder). For the past, add på: se tilbage på (look back on).

sentence.da: Hun vil **se tilbage** på sin barndom.
sentence.en: She wants to look back on her childhood.

at se tv.explanation: "At se tv" means "to watch TV". Danish uses se (to see) where English says "watch", as in se en film (to watch a film). At se fjernsyn (to watch television) means the same. Tv is said as two letters, te-ve.

sentence.da: Vi vil **se tv** i aften.
sentence.en: We want to watch TV tonight.

at se ud.explanation: "At se ud" means "to look", in the sense of how something appears: Du ser træt ud (You look tired). Hvordan ser det ud? (What does it look like?) Using your eyes is just at se (to see).

sentence.da: Min bror skal **se ud** som en pirat til festen.
sentence.en: My brother has to look like a pirate at the party.

at sejle.explanation: "At sejle" means "to sail", and it covers any trip on water, with or without sails: Vi sejler til Bornholm (We are going to Bornholm by boat). Rowing is a different word, at ro.

sentence.da: Om sommeren vil vi **sejle** til en lille ø.
sentence.en: In the summer, we want to sail to a small island.

at sende.explanation: "At sende" means "to send", for example a letter, a parcel or an email. The person who gets it comes right after sender (send), with no word for "to": Jeg sender dig en besked (I send you a message).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sende** et brev til mor.
sentence.en: I want to send a letter to Mom.

at sende en sms.explanation: "At sende en sms" means "to text", or literally to send an SMS. To say who gets it, put them after sende (send): Jeg sender dig en sms (I send you a text).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sende en sms** til min ven.
sentence.en: I want to send a text to my friend.

at servere.explanation: "At servere" means "to serve" food or drinks, for example in a restaurant or for guests at home. Maden bliver serveret klokken 18 means "The food is served at 6 pm".

sentence.da: Tjeneren vil **servere** maden nu.
sentence.en: The waiter will serve the food now.

at shoppe.explanation: "At shoppe" means "to shop", mostly for fun, like looking for clothes: Vi skal shoppe i weekenden (We are going shopping this weekend). For groceries, use at købe ind (to buy groceries).

sentence.da: Vi skal **shoppe** i byen i weekenden.
sentence.en: We are going shopping in town this weekend.

at sidde.explanation: "At sidde" means "to sit": Jeg sidder på en stol (I am sitting on a chair). Jeg sidder ved computeren means "I am sitting at the computer". To sit down is at sætte sig (literally to put oneself).

sentence.da: Du kan **sidde** på stolen.
sentence.en: You can sit on the chair.

at sidde fast.explanation: "At sidde fast" means "to be stuck", the state of not moving: Bilen sidder fast (The car is stuck). It fits a person who cannot go on: Jeg sidder fast med opgaven (I am stuck on the task).

sentence.da: Lastbilen kan **sidde fast** i mudderet.
sentence.en: The truck can end up stuck in the mud.

at sige.explanation: "At sige" means "to say": Hvad siger du? (What are you saying?). At sige hej means "to say hi". To tell a story, use at fortælle (to tell) instead.

sentence.da: Børnene skal **sige** tak.
sentence.en: The children must say thank you.

at sige farvel.explanation: "At sige farvel" means "to say goodbye". Farvel (goodbye) can sound a little final. Among friends, Danes more often say hej hej (bye bye) or vi ses (see you).

sentence.da: Vi skal **sige farvel** til vores gæster.
sentence.en: We have to say goodbye to our guests.

at sige goddag.explanation: "At sige goddag" means "to say hello", literally to say good day. Goddag is a rather formal or old-fashioned greeting. With friends, you would normally say hej (hi).

sentence.da: Du skal **sige goddag** til min mor.
sentence.en: You must say hello to my mother.

at sige op.explanation: "At sige op" means "to resign / quit": Han sagde op i går (He quit yesterday). It is also used to cancel something, like a subscription: Jeg sagde mit abonnement op (I canceled my subscription).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sige op** og finde et nyt job.
sentence.en: I want to quit and find a new job.

at sige til.explanation: "At sige til" means "to tell" or "to let know", so someone can act: Sig til, hvis du har brug for hjælp (Tell me if you need help). Jeg siger til, når maden er klar (I will let you know when the food is ready).

sentence.da: Du skal **sige til**, når du er sulten.
sentence.en: You have to let me know when you are hungry.

at sige undskyld.explanation: "At sige undskyld" means "to say sorry": Jeg sagde undskyld til hende (I said sorry to her). Undskyld alone also gets someone's attention: Undskyld, ved du, hvor stationen er? (Excuse me, do you know where the station is?)

sentence.da: Du skal **sige undskyld** til din bror.
sentence.en: You have to say sorry to your brother.

at skabe.explanation: "At skabe" means "to create", to bring something new into being: Hun skaber en god stemning (She creates a good mood). It sounds bigger than at lave (to make), so it fits ideas, art and jobs.

sentence.da: Vi vil **skabe** en ny hjemmeside sammen.
sentence.en: We want to create a new website together.

at skade.explanation: "At skade" means "to harm" or "to damage": Det skader ikke (It does no harm). It works for people and things: Regnen skadede huset (The rain damaged the house).

sentence.da: For meget sukker kan **skade** dine tænder.
sentence.en: Too much sugar can harm your teeth.

at skaffe.explanation: "At skaffe" means "to get" or "to obtain", often with some effort: Jeg skaffer en bil (I will get a car). Kan du skaffe mad til alle? (Can you get food for everyone?) Just receiving something is at få: Jeg fik en gave (I got a gift).

sentence.da: Vi kan **skaffe** billetter til dig.
sentence.en: We can get tickets for you.

at skifte.explanation: "At skifte" means "to change" by swapping one thing for another: Jeg skifter dæk (I change tires). Du skal skifte tøj (You need to change clothes). To make something different, use at ændre: Jeg ændrer planen (I am changing the plan).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skifte** tøj, når vi kommer hjem.
sentence.en: I want to change clothes when we get home.

at skifte mening.explanation: "At skifte mening" means "to change one's mind" about an opinion or a decision: Han skifter mening hele tiden (He changes his mind all the time). It is not used for changing a thing like a shirt.

sentence.da: Du kan **skifte mening**, når du vil.
sentence.en: You can change your mind whenever you want.

at skifte tøj.explanation: "At skifte tøj" means "to change clothes". At skifte on its own means "to change" or "to switch" something, such as skifte job (to change jobs).

sentence.da: Jeg er våd og vil **skifte tøj**.
sentence.en: I am wet and want to change clothes.

at skifte ud.explanation: "At skifte ud" means "to replace": you swap an old thing for a new one. Jeg skifter pæren ud (I replace the light bulb). Vi skiftede alle lamperne ud (We replaced all the lamps).

sentence.da: Træneren vil **skifte ud** midt i kampen.
sentence.en: The coach wants to substitute in the middle of the game.

at skille.explanation: "At skille" means "to separate", to pull two things apart: Jeg skiller sort tøj fra hvidt (I separate black clothes from white). It is also used for divorce: De blev skilt (They got divorced).

sentence.da: Du skal **skille** æggeblommen fra hviden.
sentence.en: You have to separate the yolk from the white.

at skilles.explanation: "At skilles" means "to separate", and for a couple "to divorce": Mine forældre skiltes, da jeg var lille (My parents divorced when I was small). It also means parting ways: Vi skilles ved stationen (We part at the station).

sentence.da: Mine forældre vil **skilles**, men de er venner.
sentence.en: My parents want to get divorced, but they are friends.

at skinne.explanation: "At skinne" means "to shine": Solen skinner i dag (The sun is shining today). It also works for people who look happy: Hun skinner af glæde (She glows with joy).

sentence.da: Solen vil **skinne** hele weekenden.
sentence.en: The sun will shine all weekend.

at skjule.explanation: "At skjule" means "to hide", so others cannot see or find something: Han skjuler gaven (He is hiding the gift). It also works for feelings: Hun skjuler sin vrede (She is hiding her anger).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skjule** pakken under sengen.
sentence.en: I will hide the package under the bed.

at skrige.explanation: "At skrige" means "to scream", often from fear, pain or anger: Hun skreg af skræk (She screamed in fright). For loud but normal calling, use at råbe (to shout).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **skrige** højt, når jeg er bange.
sentence.en: I can scream loudly when I am scared.

at skrive.explanation: "At skrive" means "to write": Jeg skriver et brev (I am writing a letter). It also covers typing and texting: skrive en besked (to write a message).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skrive** et brev til mor.
sentence.en: I want to write a letter to Mom.

at skrive ned.explanation: "At skrive ned" means "to write down", to keep something on paper so you remember it: Skriv det ned, så du ikke glemmer det (Write it down so you do not forget it).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skrive ned**, hvad han siger.
sentence.en: I want to write down what he says.

at skrive til.explanation: "At skrive til" means "to write to" a person: Jeg skriver til min bedstemor (I am writing to my grandmother). It also covers texting: Skriv til mig! (Text me!).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skrive til** min lærer i dag.
sentence.en: I want to write to my teacher today.

at skrue.explanation: "At skrue" means "to screw", to turn a screw in or out: Han skruer låget af (He unscrews the lid). With op (up) or ned (down) it means to turn something up or down: Skru ned for musikken (Turn down the music).

sentence.da: Kan du **skrue** hylden fast på væggen?
sentence.en: Can you screw the shelf onto the wall?

at skrælle.explanation: "At skrælle" means "to peel", for potatoes, carrots and fruit: Jeg skræller kartoflerne (I peel the potatoes). The skin you take off is en skræl (a peel).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **skrælle** fem kartofler.
sentence.en: I have to peel five potatoes.

at skræmme.explanation: "At skræmme" means "to scare": Du skræmte mig! (You scared me!) To be scared yourself, say at være bange: Jeg er bange for edderkopper (I am scared of spiders).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **skræmme** katten.
sentence.en: You must not scare the cat.

at skubbe.explanation: "At skubbe" means "to push": Vi skubber bilen (We are pushing the car). It works for people too: Han skubbede mig (He pushed me). On a door, the sign says Skub (Push).

sentence.da: Kan du **skubbe** bilen sammen med mig?
sentence.en: Can you push the car together with me?

at skuffe.explanation: "At skuffe" means "to disappoint": Filmen skuffede mig (The movie disappointed me). Du skuffer mig! (You are disappointing me!) sounds strong and personal.

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **skuffe** dig igen.
sentence.en: I do not want to disappoint you again.

at skulle.explanation: "At skulle" means "to have to" or "should": Jeg skal arbejde (I have to work). It is also used for plans: Jeg skal i skole (I am going to school).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **skulle** arbejde i morgen.
sentence.en: I don't want to have to work tomorrow.

at skyde.explanation: "At skyde" means "to shoot": Jægeren skyder en hare (The hunter shoots a hare). It is also used in sports: Han skød bolden i mål (He shot the ball into the goal).

sentence.da: Hun kan **skyde** med bue og pil.
sentence.en: She can shoot with a bow and arrow.

at skylde.explanation: "At skylde" means "to owe": Jeg skylder dig hundrede kroner (I owe you a hundred kroner). With på (on) it means "to blame": Han skylder på mig (He blames me).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **skylde** nogen penge.
sentence.en: I do not want to owe anyone money.

at skynde sig.explanation: "At skynde sig" means "to hurry". The little word after it follows who hurries: Jeg skynder mig (I hurry), Han skynder sig (He hurries). Skynd dig! means "Hurry up!"

sentence.da: Hun må **skynde sig**, fordi toget kører snart.
sentence.en: She has to hurry because the train leaves soon.

at skåle.explanation: "At skåle" means "to toast", raising your glass and drinking together: Vi skåler for dig (We toast you). It also works for things: Vi skåler for den nye lejlighed (We toast the new apartment).

sentence.da: Nu skal vi alle **skåle** for fødselaren.
sentence.en: Now we are all going to toast the birthday person.

at skændes.explanation: "At skændes" means "to argue", and it takes two or more people: Vi skændes aldrig (We never argue). To say who with, add med: Jeg skændes med min bror (I am arguing with my brother).

sentence.da: Børnene **skændes** hele tiden om legetøjet.
sentence.en: The children argue all the time about the toy.

at skære.explanation: "At skære" means "to cut" with a knife: Jeg skærer brødet i stykker (I cut the bread into pieces). Cutting hair with scissors is a different word, at klippe (to cut with scissors).

sentence.da: Kan du **skære** løget for mig?
sentence.en: Can you cut the onion for me?

at slappe af.explanation: "At slappe af" means "to relax" or "to take it easy", like resting on the sofa after a long day. Slap af! (Relax!) can also tell someone to calm down. The little word af (off) stays in every form.

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og vil **slappe af**.
sentence.en: I am tired and want to relax.

at slette.explanation: "At slette" means "to delete", to remove something from a device, like a file or a message: Jeg sletter den gamle fil (I delete the old file).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **slette** alle de gamle billeder.
sentence.en: I want to delete all the old photos.

at slippe.explanation: "At slippe" means "to let go" and "to escape": Slip mig! (Let go of me!) Han slap væk (He got away). Slippe for means "to be spared from": Jeg slap for at vaske op (I got out of doing the dishes).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **slippe** snoren nu.
sentence.en: You must not let go of the string now.

at slippe af med.explanation: "At slippe af med" means "to get rid of": Hun slap af med sin forkølelse (She got rid of her cold). It works for things you do not want and for problems.

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **slippe af med** min gamle sofa.
sentence.en: I would like to get rid of my old sofa.

at sluge.explanation: "At sluge" means "to swallow", to send food or a pill down your throat: Hun slugte tabletten uden vand (She swallowed the pill without water). It can also mean "to gulp down": Han slugte maden på to minutter (He gulped the food down in two minutes).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **sluge** den store tablet.
sentence.en: I cannot swallow the big pill.

at slukke.explanation: "At slukke" means "to turn off" a light or "to put out" a fire: slukke lyset (turn off the light) and slukke en brand (put out a fire). For a TV or the radio, use slukke for (turn off): slukke for fjernsynet (turn off the TV).

sentence.da: Husk at **slukke** lyset.
sentence.en: Remember to turn off the light.

at slukke for.explanation: "At slukke for" means "to turn off" something like the TV, the radio or the heating: Jeg slukker for radioen (I turn off the radio). For a light, slukke lyset (turn off the light) is the usual choice. A fire is put out with plain slukke: slukke en brand (to put out a fire).

sentence.da: Husk at **slukke for** fjernsynet.
sentence.en: Remember to turn off the TV.

at slutte.explanation: "At slutte" means "to end" or "to finish": Skolen slutter klokken tre (School ends at three). With med (with) it means "to stop doing something": Jeg slutter med at ryge (I am quitting smoking).

sentence.da: Filmen skal **slutte** om en time.
sentence.en: The movie is going to end in an hour.

at slå.explanation: "At slå" means "to hit" and "to beat", so it covers hitting with your hand or a tool and winning over someone: Hun slog mig i skak (She beat me at chess). Slå græsset means "mow the lawn".

sentence.da: Jeg kan **slå** et søm i væggen med en hammer.
sentence.en: I can hit a nail into the wall with a hammer.

at slå græs.explanation: "At slå græs" means "to mow the lawn". It is built from slå (hit) and græs (grass), with no word for the: Han slår græs hver weekend (He mows the lawn every weekend).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **slå græs**, fordi græsset er blevet langt.
sentence.en: I have to mow the lawn because the grass has gotten long.

at slå op.explanation: "At slå op" means "to look up" a word: Jeg slår ordet op (I look up the word). It can also mean to break up: Hun slog op med ham (She broke up with him).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **slå op** i ordbogen.
sentence.en: I have to look it up in the dictionary.

at smage.explanation: "At smage" means "to taste", both for trying food and for having a flavor. Det smager godt means "It tastes good" and "Det smager af citron" means "It tastes of lemon".

sentence.da: Må jeg **smage** din suppe?
sentence.en: May I taste your soup?

at smelte.explanation: "At smelte" means "to melt", when something solid turns to liquid: Isen smelter i solen (The ice melts in the sun). You can also melt something yourself: Jeg smelter smør (I melt butter).

sentence.da: Sneen vil **smelte**, når det bliver varmt.
sentence.en: The snow will melt when it gets warm.

at smide.explanation: "At smide" means "to throw", and also "to throw away": Jeg smider papiret i skraldespanden (I throw the paper in the trash can). For throwing a ball, kaste (throw) is more usual.

sentence.da: Du må ikke **smide** affald på gaden.
sentence.en: You must not throw trash on the street.

at smide ud.explanation: "At smide ud" means "to throw out", like old food or things you no longer need: Jeg smider maden ud (I throw the food out). It also means "to kick out" of a place: De smed ham ud af baren (They threw him out of the bar).

sentence.da: Vi skal **smide ud**, hvad vi ikke bruger.
sentence.en: We have to throw out what we do not use.

at smile.explanation: "At smile" means "to smile". Hun smilede til mig means "She smiled at me": you smile til (to) someone.

sentence.da: Hun er glad og kan **smile** til alle.
sentence.en: She is happy and can smile at everyone.

at sminke sig.explanation: "At sminke sig" means "to put on makeup": Hun sminker sig hver morgen (She puts on makeup every morning). The little word after it changes with the person: jeg sminker mig (I put on makeup).

sentence.da: Hun vil **sminke sig** og tage en kjole på.
sentence.en: She wants to put on makeup and put on a dress.

at smutte.explanation: "At smutte" means "to pop out" or "to slip away" quickly: Jeg smutter lige ud (I'll just pop out). It can also mean "to slip" by accident: Kniven smuttede (The knife slipped).

forms.en: I have slipped away / popped out

sentence.da: Jeg vil lige **smutte** ned i supermarkedet.
sentence.en: I'll just pop down to the supermarket.

at smøre.explanation: "At smøre" means "to spread", for example butter on bread: Jeg smører smør på brødet (I spread butter on the bread). Danes also say at smøre en madpakke (to make a packed lunch).

sentence.da: Kan du **smøre** et stykke brød til mig?
sentence.en: Can you spread a piece of bread for me?

at snakke.explanation: "At snakke" means "to talk" or "to chat", and it is the everyday word for speaking. Kan vi snakke sammen? means "Can we talk?". At tale (to speak) is a bit more formal.

sentence.da: Jeg har tid og kan **snakke** nu.
sentence.en: I have time and can talk now.

at snakke om.explanation: "At snakke om" means "to talk about": Vi snakker om mad (We are talking about food). To talk with a person, use med (with): Jeg snakker med min mor (I talk with my mother).

sentence.da: Vi vil **snakke om** vores ferie i aften.
sentence.en: We want to talk about our vacation tonight.

at snakke om vejret.explanation: "At snakke om vejret" means "to make small talk", literally "to talk about the weather": Vi snakkede om vejret i elevatoren (We made small talk in the elevator). It is chat where nothing important is said.

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke bare **snakke om vejret** med dig.
sentence.en: I don't just want to make small talk with you.

at sne.explanation: "At sne" means "to snow": Det sner (It is snowing). The word for snow itself is also "sne", as in Der er sne (There is snow), so the sentence shows which one is meant.

sentence.da: I vinter kan det **sne** meget.
sentence.en: In winter it can snow a lot.

at snooze.explanation: "At snooze" means "to snooze", to press the button on your alarm for a few more minutes of sleep: Jeg snoozer to gange hver morgen (I hit snooze twice every morning). To sleep late on purpose, say at sove længe (to sleep in).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **snooze** i fem minutter mere.
sentence.en: I want to snooze for five more minutes.

at snorke.explanation: "At snorke" means "to snore": Han snorker højt om natten (He snores loudly at night). To tell someone to stop, say Hold op med at snorke! (Stop snoring!)

sentence.da: Min far plejer at **snorke** meget højt.
sentence.en: My dad usually snores very loudly.

at sortere.explanation: "At sortere" means "to sort", to put things into groups or an order, like trash into bins or mail into piles: Jeg sorterer affaldet (I sort the trash).

sentence.da: Vi skal **sortere** tøjet efter farve.
sentence.en: We have to sort the clothes by color.

at sove.explanation: "At sove" means "to sleep": Jeg sover godt (I sleep well). Going to bed is a different phrase: at gå i seng (to go to bed). Sov godt means "Sleep well".

sentence.da: Børnene er trætte og vil **sove**.
sentence.en: The children are tired and want to sleep.

at sove længe.explanation: "At sove længe" means "to sleep in": Vi sover længe i weekenden (We sleep in on the weekend). Længe means "a long time", so Hun sov længe (She slept for a long time) works too.

sentence.da: I morgen er det lørdag, og jeg vil **sove længe**.
sentence.en: Tomorrow is Saturday, and I want to sleep in.

at sove over sig.explanation: "At sove over sig" means "to oversleep", to sleep past the time you meant to get up: Jeg sov over mig og kom for sent (I overslept and was late). To sleep late on purpose, say at sove længe (to sleep in).

sentence.da: Hun vil ikke **sove over sig** i morgen.
sentence.en: She does not want to oversleep tomorrow.

at spare.explanation: "At spare" means "to save", mostly money: Vi sparer penge til en rejse (We are saving money for a trip). It also works for time: Det sparer tid (That saves time).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spare** penge til en ny cykel.
sentence.en: I want to save money for a new bike.

at spare op.explanation: "At spare op" means "to save up", to put money aside bit by bit for something: Jeg sparer op til en cykel (I am saving up for a bike). Without op (up), at spare is the general word for saving, as in at spare tid (to save time).

sentence.da: Hver måned vil jeg **spare op** tusind kroner.
sentence.en: Every month I want to save up a thousand kroner.

at spare på.explanation: "At spare på" means "to save on", as in using less of something: Vi sparer på varmen (We are saving on heat). It also means "to be careful with": Hun sparer på pengene (She is careful with the money).

sentence.da: Vi skal **spare på** strømmen i vinter.
sentence.en: We have to save on electricity this winter.

at sparke.explanation: "At sparke" means "to kick": Han sparkede bolden over hegnet (He kicked the ball over the fence). With til (to), you give something a kick: Hun sparkede til døren (She gave the door a kick).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **sparke** bolden i mål.
sentence.en: The kids want to kick the ball into the goal.

at spilde.explanation: "At spilde" means "to spill" and "to waste": Jeg spildte vand på bordet (I spilled water on the table). Vi må ikke spilde mad (We must not waste food).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **spilde** min tid på det.
sentence.en: I do not want to waste my time on that.

at spilde tid.explanation: "At spilde tid" means "to waste time": Jeg spilder tid på telefonen (I waste time on the phone). At spilde on its own also means "to spill": Jeg spildte kaffe (I spilled coffee).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **spilde tid** på det her.
sentence.en: I do not want to waste time on this.

at spille.explanation: "At spille" means "to play" a game, a sport or an instrument: Jeg spiller guitar (I play the guitar) and Vi spiller fodbold (We play soccer). It also means "to act" a part. For children playing for fun, Danes say at lege (to play).

sentence.da: Min bror kan **spille** guitar og synge.
sentence.en: My brother can play the guitar and sing.

at spille en rolle.explanation: "At spille en rolle" means "to play a role", on stage or in real life: Hun spiller en rolle i skolens teater (She plays a role in the school theater). It also means "to matter": Prisen spiller ikke nogen rolle (The price does not matter).

sentence.da: Han vil gerne **spille en rolle** i filmen.
sentence.en: He would like to play a role in the film.

at spille fodbold.explanation: "At spille fodbold" means "to play soccer" ("football" in Britain). Spille (to play) is used for most games and sports. The word fodbold is built from fod (foot) and bold (ball), and there is no en (a) before it.

sentence.da: Børnene vil **spille fodbold** i dag.
sentence.en: The children want to play soccer today.

at spise.explanation: "At spise" means "to eat": Vi spiser aftensmad (We eat dinner). At spise ude means "to eat out". For drinking, use at drikke (to drink).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spise** brød, ost og æbler.
sentence.en: I want to eat bread, cheese and apples.

at springe.explanation: "At springe" means "to jump": Børn springer i vandet (Children jump into the water). With over (over) added, it means "to skip": Jeg springer en side over (I skip a page).

sentence.da: Hunden kan **springe** over hegnet.
sentence.en: The dog can jump over the fence.

at springe over.explanation: "At springe over" means "to skip", to leave something out: Jeg springer frokosten over (I skip lunch). It can also mean "to jump over": Hunden sprang over hegnet (The dog jumped over the fence).

sentence.da: Jeg vil aldrig **springe over** morgenmaden.
sentence.en: I will never skip breakfast.

at sprøjte.explanation: "At sprøjte" means "to spray" or "to squirt": Han sprøjter vand på blomsterne (He sprays water on the flowers). A doctor's needle is en sprøjte (a syringe), the same word.

sentence.da: Børnene vil **sprøjte** vand på hinanden.
sentence.en: The children want to spray water on each other.

at spænde.explanation: "At spænde" means "to tighten" and "to fasten": Spænd remmen (Tighten the strap). It also means to tense up: Jeg spænder musklerne (I tense my muscles).

sentence.da: Du skal altid **spænde** sikkerhedsbæltet i bilen.
sentence.en: You must always fasten the seat belt in the car.

at spørge.explanation: "At spørge" means "to ask" a question: Jeg spørger ham om vejen (I ask him for directions). To ask for something you want, use at bede om (to ask for): Jeg beder om en kop kaffe (I ask for a cup of coffee).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spørge** læreren.
sentence.en: I want to ask the teacher.

at spørge om.explanation: "At spørge om" means "to ask about" or "to ask for". Om (about) comes right after spørge and is followed by the topic or thing you want: spørge om prisen (ask about the price), spørge om vej (ask for directions).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spørge om** hjælp.
sentence.en: I want to ask for help.

at spørge om vej.explanation: "At spørge om vej" means "to ask for directions", literally to ask about way: Undskyld, må jeg spørge om vej? (Excuse me, may I ask for directions?).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spørge om vej** til banegården.
sentence.en: I want to ask for directions to the station.

at standse.explanation: "At standse" means "to stop", when something moving comes to a halt or you make it halt: Bilen standsede foran huset (The car stopped in front of the house). To quit doing something, say at holde op (to quit): Jeg holder op med at ryge (I am quitting smoking).

sentence.da: Bussen skal **standse** ved stationen.
sentence.en: The bus has to stop at the station.

at starte.explanation: "At starte" means "to start", for people and for machines: Bilen starter ikke (The car won't start) and Vi starter i morgen (We start tomorrow). At begynde (to begin) means almost the same.

sentence.da: Filmen skal **starte** klokken otte.
sentence.en: The movie is going to start at eight.

at starte på.explanation: "At starte på" means "to start on" something, like a task: Jeg starter på opgaven (I start on the assignment). Without på (on), starte (to start) is for things that get going: Bilen starter ikke (The car won't start).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **starte på** et nyt projekt i dag.
sentence.en: I want to start on a new project today.

at stave.explanation: "At stave" means "to spell", saying the letters of a word one at a time. It is common when you give a name or an address on the phone: Hvordan staver man det? (How do you spell that?)

sentence.da: Kan du **stave** dit navn?
sentence.en: Can you spell your name?

at stege.explanation: "At stege" means "to fry" and "to roast": Jeg steger kød i panden (I fry meat in the pan) and Vi steger en and i ovnen (We roast a duck in the oven). Cooking in water is at koge (to boil).

forms.en: I have fried, I have roasted

sentence.da: Jeg skal **stege** æggene i panden.
sentence.en: I am going to fry the eggs in the pan.

at stemme.explanation: "At stemme" means "to vote": Jeg stemmer på ham (I vote for him). It also means "to be correct": Det stemmer! (That is right!)

sentence.da: Alle over atten år kan **stemme** ved valget.
sentence.en: Everyone over eighteen can vote in the election.

at stemme på.explanation: "At stemme på" means "to vote for" the person or party you choose. Danish uses på (on) where English says for: Vi stemte på Peter (We voted for Peter). Without på, stemme (to vote) just means casting a vote.

sentence.da: Til valget vil jeg **stemme på** Anna.
sentence.en: At the election, I want to vote for Anna.

at stige.explanation: "At stige" means "to rise" and "to climb": Prisen stiger (The price is rising). Han stiger op ad trappen (He climbs up the stairs). With vehicles, it means "to get in": Hun steg ind i bilen (She got into the car).

sentence.da: Temperaturen kan **stige** til tredive grader.
sentence.en: The temperature can rise to thirty degrees.

at stige af.explanation: "At stige af" means "to get off", a bus, a train or a bike: Hun stiger af cyklen (She gets off the bike). The opposite is at stige på (to get on).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **stige af** bussen ved torvet.
sentence.en: I will get off the bus at the square.

at stige på.explanation: "At stige på" means "to get on", a bus, a train or a bike: Vi stiger på toget i Odense (We get on the train in Odense). The opposite is at stige af (to get off).

sentence.da: Vi må **stige på** bussen nu.
sentence.en: We have to get on the bus now.

at stikke.explanation: "At stikke" means "to sting" and "to stick": Bien stak mig (The bee stung me). It also means to put something in: Jeg stikker pengene i lommen (I stick the money in my pocket).

sentence.da: Du skal **stikke** nøglen i døren.
sentence.en: You have to stick the key in the door.

at stikke af.explanation: "At stikke af" means "to run off": you get away quickly, often from trouble. Tyven stak af (The thief ran off). Hunden stak af (The dog ran off).

sentence.da: Drengen ville **stikke af**, men læreren så ham.
sentence.en: The boy wanted to run off, but the teacher saw him.

at stille.explanation: "At stille" means "to put / place (upright)": Jeg stiller cyklen i skuret (I put the bike in the shed). For something lying flat, use at lægge (to lay): Jeg lægger bogen på bordet (I put the book on the table).

sentence.da: Kan du **stille** flasken på bordet?
sentence.en: Can you put the bottle on the table?

at stille et spørgsmål.explanation: "At stille et spørgsmål" means "to ask a question": Læreren stillede et spørgsmål (The teacher asked a question). The short word at spørge (to ask) is also common: Jeg vil spørge dig om noget (I want to ask you something).

sentence.da: Må jeg **stille et spørgsmål** om lektien?
sentence.en: May I ask a question about the homework?

at stille uret.explanation: "At stille uret" means "to set the clock". You can say which way: stille uret en time frem (set the clock an hour forward) or stille uret en time tilbage (set the clock an hour back).

sentence.da: Vi skal **stille uret** en time tilbage.
sentence.en: We have to set the clock back an hour.

at stjæle.explanation: "At stjæle" means "to steal": Han stjal min cykel (He stole my bike). Robbing a bank or a person is different: at røve (to rob).

sentence.da: Man må ikke **stjæle** fra andre.
sentence.en: You must not steal from others.

at stole på.explanation: "At stole på" means "to trust", and på always stays with it: Jeg stoler på min læge (I trust my doctor). Jeg stoler ikke på ham (I do not trust him).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **stole på** min bedste ven.
sentence.en: I can trust my best friend.

at stoppe.explanation: "At stoppe" means "to stop": Bussen stopper her (The bus stops here). With med (with) it means "to quit doing something": Jeg stopper med at spise slik (I am quitting eating sweets).

sentence.da: Bilen skal **stoppe** ved det røde lys.
sentence.en: The car has to stop at the red light.

at streame.explanation: "At streame" means "to stream", to watch or listen online without saving the file: Vi streamer en serie hver aften (We stream a series every evening).

sentence.da: Vi vil **streame** en film i aften.
sentence.en: We want to stream a movie tonight.

at strikke.explanation: "At strikke" means "to knit": Min mor strikker en hue (My mother is knitting a hat). Crocheting is a different word: at hækle (to crochet).

sentence.da: Min mormor kan **strikke** en varm trøje.
sentence.en: My grandmother can knit a warm sweater.

at stryge.explanation: "At stryge" means "to iron" clothes: Jeg stryger en skjorte (I iron a shirt). It also means "to stroke" something gently: Hun stryger katten (She strokes the cat).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **stryge** en skjorte før mødet.
sentence.en: I have to iron a shirt before the meeting.

at strække.explanation: "At strække" means "to stretch": Jeg strækker armene (I stretch my arms). To stretch your own body, add sig (oneself): Katten strækker sig (The cat stretches).

sentence.da: Det er vigtigt at **strække** benene efter løbeturen.
sentence.en: It is important to stretch your legs after the run.

at strække sig.explanation: "At strække sig" means "to stretch" your own body: Han strækker sig efter træning (He stretches after exercise). The little word at the end changes with who stretches: vi strækker os (we stretch).

sentence.da: Katten vil **strække sig** i solen.
sentence.en: The cat wants to stretch in the sun.

at studere.explanation: "At studere" means "to study", especially at a university: Jeg studerer historie (I study history). For studying at home for a test, Danes often say at læse til en eksamen (literally to read for an exam).

related.en: a study, a course of study

sentence.da: Hun vil **studere** medicin på universitetet.
sentence.en: She wants to study medicine at the university.

at styre.explanation: "At styre" means "to steer" and "to control": Hun styrer bilen (She steers the car). It also means "to run" something: Han styrer firmaet (He runs the company).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **styre** båden selv.
sentence.en: I can steer the boat myself.

at stå.explanation: "At stå" means "to stand", but Danish uses it more widely than English: Flasken står på bordet (The bottle is on the table). It also covers writing: Der står et navn på døren (A name is written on the door).

sentence.da: Man kan **stå** eller sidde i bussen.
sentence.en: You can stand or sit on the bus.

at stå af.explanation: "At stå af" means "to get off", used for a bus, a train or the metro: Hvor skal vi stå af? (Where do we get off?) For a bike or a horse, use at stige af (to get off).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **stå af** ved næste stop.
sentence.en: I will get off at the next stop.

at stå for.explanation: "At stå for" means "to be in charge of", a job or a task: Hvem står for festen? (Who is in charge of the party?) Jeg står for musikken (I am in charge of the music).

forms.en: I have been in charge of

sentence.da: Min bror vil **stå for** maden til festen.
sentence.en: My brother will be in charge of the food for the party.

at stå i kø.explanation: "At stå i kø" means "to stand in line" (or "to queue"), literally to stand in queue: Jeg står i kø i supermarkedet (I am standing in line at the supermarket).

sentence.da: Vi må **stå i kø** for billetter.
sentence.en: We have to stand in line for tickets.

at stå op.explanation: "At stå op" means "to get up" out of bed, literally to stand up. When saying what you have done, Danish uses er (am) instead of har (have): Jeg er stået op (I have gotten up). To stand up from a chair, Danes say at rejse sig (to stand up).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **stå op** klokken syv.
sentence.en: I want to get up at seven.

at stå på ski.explanation: "At stå på ski" means "to ski", literally to stand on skis. Water skiing works the same way: at stå på vandski (to water ski). There is no en or et (a) before ski.

sentence.da: Vi vil **stå på ski** i Norge.
sentence.en: We want to ski in Norway.

at støtte.explanation: "At støtte" means "to support" a person or a cause: Mine forældre støtter mig (My parents support me). It also means "to lean on": Han støttede sig til væggen (He leaned on the wall).

sentence.da: Jeg vil altid **støtte** dig.
sentence.en: I will always support you.

at støvsuge.explanation: "At støvsuge" means "to vacuum". It is built from støv (dust) and suge (suck): Han støvsuger trappen (He vacuums the stairs). The machine is en støvsuger (a vacuum cleaner).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **støvsuge** stuen i dag.
sentence.en: I have to vacuum the living room today.

at suge.explanation: "At suge" means "to suck", pulling something in with your mouth or a machine: Babyen suger på sutten (The baby sucks on the pacifier).

sentence.da: Barnet kan **suge** saften op med et sugerør.
sentence.en: The child can suck the juice up with a straw.

at sukke.explanation: "At sukke" means "to sigh", letting out a deep breath when you are tired, sad or annoyed: Hun sukkede dybt (She sighed deeply). A sigh is et suk.

sentence.da: Min bror kan **sukke** højt, når han keder sig.
sentence.en: My brother can sigh loudly when he is bored.

at svare.explanation: "At svare" means "to answer" or "to reply". To answer a question, add på (on): svare på et spørgsmål (to answer a question).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **svare** på spørgsmålet.
sentence.en: I can answer the question.

at svare på.explanation: "At svare på" means "to answer" or "to reply to", and på always follows the thing you answer: Jeg svarer på din besked (I reply to your message).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **svare på** din mail i morgen.
sentence.en: I will reply to your email tomorrow.

at svede.explanation: "At svede" means "to sweat": Jeg sveder, når jeg løber (I sweat when I run). It also fits nerves: Hun sveder over eksamen (She is sweating over the exam).

sentence.da: Når det er varmt, kan jeg **svede** meget.
sentence.en: When it is hot, I can sweat a lot.

at svømme.explanation: "At svømme" means "to swim": Jeg svømmer i havet (I swim in the sea). For a quick dip, Danes also say at bade (to go for a swim): Vi bader i søen (We are going for a swim in the lake).

sentence.da: Fisk kan **svømme** i vandet.
sentence.en: Fish can swim in the water.

at sy.explanation: "At sy" means "to sew": Jeg syr en knap på (I am sewing on a button). It also covers closing a cut with stitches: Lægen syede såret (The doctor stitched the wound).

sentence.da: Min mor kan **sy** sine egne kjoler.
sentence.en: My mother can sew her own dresses.

at sygemelde sig.explanation: "At sygemelde sig" means "to call in sick", telling your employer that you are ill: Jeg sygemelder mig i dag (I am calling in sick today).

sentence.da: Hun må **sygemelde sig**, fordi hun har feber.
sentence.en: She has to call in sick because she has a fever.

at synes.explanation: "At synes" means "to think", in the sense of having an opinion: Jeg synes, det er godt (I think it is good). For a guess about a fact, use at tro (to believe, to guess): Jeg tror, han kommer (I think he is coming). Hvad synes du? means "What do you think?".

sentence.da: Hvad **synes** du om maden?
sentence.en: What do you think about the food?

at synge.explanation: "At synge" means "to sing". To sing along with others or with a recording, add med (with): Jeg synger med (I sing along).

sentence.da: Hun kan **synge** en smuk sang.
sentence.en: She can sing a beautiful song.

at synke.explanation: "At synke" means "to sink" and also "to swallow": Skibet synker (The ship sinks). Jeg kan ikke synke (I can't swallow).

sentence.da: Den tunge sten vil **synke** i vandet.
sentence.en: The heavy stone will sink in the water.

at sælge.explanation: "At sælge" means "to sell". Til salg means "for sale", as on a sign: Bilen er til salg (The car is for sale).

sentence.da: Bageren vil **sælge** brød i butikken.
sentence.en: The baker wants to sell bread in the shop.

at sætte.explanation: "At sætte" means "to put" or "to place" something somewhere: Jeg sætter bogen på hylden (I put the book on the shelf). Do not mix it up with at sidde (to sit), which describes where you already are. Sæt dig means "Sit down".

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sætte** koppen på bordet.
sentence.en: I want to put the cup on the table.

at sætte i gang.explanation: "At sætte i gang" means "to start" or "to launch", to get something running: Vi sætter projektet i gang (We are launching the project). The thing itself gets going: Projektet kommer i gang (The project gets going).

sentence.da: Når I er klar, vil jeg **sætte i gang**.
sentence.en: When you are ready, I will get things started.

at sætte ind.explanation: "At sætte ind" means "to put in", and also "to deposit": Jeg sætter pengene ind på kontoen (I put the money into the account). It can mean "to put into service": Vi sætter flere busser ind (We are putting more buses into service).

sentence.da: Jeg går i banken for at **sætte ind**.
sentence.en: I am going to the bank to make a deposit.

at sætte pris på.explanation: "At sætte pris på" means "to appreciate", to value what someone does or gives: Jeg sætter pris på din hjælp (I appreciate your help). Add stor (big) for more: Jeg sætter stor pris på det (I really appreciate it).

sentence.da: Man skal **sætte pris på** sine venner.
sentence.en: You should appreciate your friends.

at sætte på.explanation: "At sætte på" means "to put on" for music, a pot or the heat: Jeg sætter kaffe på (I am putting coffee on). For clothes, use at tage tøj på (to put on clothes).

sentence.da: Skal jeg **sætte på**, så vi kan få te?
sentence.en: Shall I put the kettle on so we can have tea?

at sætte sig.explanation: "At sætte sig" means "to sit down": Jeg sætter mig i sofaen (I sit down on the sofa). To say you are already sitting, use at sidde (to sit): Jeg sidder i sofaen (I am sitting on the sofa).

sentence.da: Han vil **sætte sig** på stolen.
sentence.en: He wants to sit down on the chair.

at søge.explanation: "At søge" means "to apply" and "to search": Jeg søger et job (I am applying for a job). To look for a thing, add efter: Jeg søger efter mine nøgler (I am looking for my keys).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **søge** et nyt job i København.
sentence.en: I want to apply for a new job in Copenhagen.

at søge efter.explanation: "At søge efter" means "to search for" something you want to find: Jeg søger efter mine nøgler (I am searching for my keys). Without efter, at søge is used to apply: Hun søger et job (She is applying for a job).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **søge efter** en billig lejlighed.
sentence.en: I want to search for a cheap apartment.

at søge ind på.explanation: "At søge ind på" means "to apply to" a school or a study program: Hun søger ind på universitetet (She is applying to the university). To apply for a job, say at søge et job (to apply for a job).

sentence.da: Min søster vil **søge ind på** universitetet i år.
sentence.en: My sister wants to apply to the university this year.

at søge job.explanation: "At søge job" means "to apply for a job", and also "to look for work": Jeg søger job som lærer (I am looking for a job as a teacher). For one specific position, say at søge en stilling (to apply for a position).

forms.en: I have applied for a job

sentence.da: Jeg vil **søge job** i en bank.
sentence.en: I want to apply for a job at a bank.

at søge om.explanation: "At søge om" means "to apply for", when you ask for something official: søge om tilladelse (apply for a permit), søge om støtte (apply for support). For a job, say at søge (to apply): søge et job (apply for a job).

sentence.da: Han skal **søge om** et visum i dag.
sentence.en: He has to apply for a visa today.

at sørge for.explanation: "At sørge for" means "to take care of" something: Jeg sørger for maden (I'll take care of the food). It also means "to make sure": Sørg for at låse døren (Make sure you lock the door).

forms.en: to make sure / take care of
I make sure / take care of
I made sure / took care of
I have made sure / taken care of

sentence.da: Jeg skal **sørge for** børnene i aften.
sentence.en: I'll take care of the children tonight.

en sag.explanation: "En sag" means "a matter" or "a case": Det er en vigtig sag (It is an important matter). At work or in court, it is a case: Advokaten arbejder på en sag (The lawyer is working on a case).

sentence.da: Politiet arbejder på en vigtig **sag**.
sentence.en: The police are working on an important case.

en saks.explanation: "En saks" means "a pair of scissors". Danish treats it as one thing: Kan jeg låne din saks? (Can I borrow your scissors?)

sentence.da: Jeg klipper papir med en **saks**.
sentence.en: I cut paper with a pair of scissors.

en sal.explanation: "En sal" means "a hall", a large room for meetings, parties or shows: Der er plads til hundrede i salen (There is room for a hundred in the hall). It is not a hallway; that is en gang (a hallway).

sentence.da: Koncerten foregår i den store **sal**.
sentence.en: The concert takes place in the big hall.

en salat.explanation: "En salat" means "a salad" and also "lettuce", so the situation tells you which one is meant. En grøn salat means "a green salad".

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **salat** med tomat og agurk.
sentence.en: I eat a salad with tomato and cucumber.

en saltbøsse.explanation: "En saltbøsse" means "a salt shaker", the small container you shake salt from at the table: Kan du række mig saltbøssen? (Can you pass me the salt shaker?)

sentence.da: Jeg ryster salt på maden fra en **saltbøsse**.
sentence.en: I shake salt onto the food from a salt shaker.

en samtale.explanation: "En samtale" means "a conversation". It is built from sam- (together) and tale (talk), so it is people talking together: Vi havde en lang samtale (We had a long conversation).

sentence.da: To mennesker har en **samtale**, når de taler sammen.
sentence.en: Two people have a conversation when they talk together.

en sandal.explanation: "En sandal" means "a sandal". Sandals come in pairs, so you will often see et par sandaler (a pair of sandals).

sentence.da: En **sandal** er en åben sko til sommer.
sentence.en: A sandal is an open shoe for summer.

en sandhed.explanation: "En sandhed" means "a truth": Det er den rene sandhed (It is the plain truth). It is built from sand (true), as in Det er sandt (That is true).

sentence.da: Der er en **sandhed** i det, han siger.
sentence.en: There is a truth in what he says.

en sandkasse.explanation: "En sandkasse" means "a sandbox", where children play with sand: Børnene leger i sandkassen (The children play in the sandbox). It is built from sand (sand) and kasse (box).

sentence.da: Barnet graver med en spade i en **sandkasse**.
sentence.en: The child digs with a shovel in a sandbox.

en sandstrand.explanation: "En sandstrand" means "a sandy beach". It is built from sand (sand) and strand (beach). Vi sad på sandstranden hele dagen (We sat on the sandy beach all day).

sentence.da: Børnene leger på den lange **sandstrand**.
sentence.en: The children play on the long sandy beach.

en sandwich.explanation: "En sandwich" means "a sandwich", bread with a filling, closed on top. Smørrebrød (open sandwich) has no top slice of bread.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **sandwich** med ost og skinke.
sentence.en: I eat a sandwich with cheese and ham.

en sang.explanation: "En sang" means "a song", music with words to sing: Vi lytter til en sang (We listen to a song). For music with no words, say et stykke musik (a piece of music).

sentence.da: Hun synger en smuk **sang** for os.
sentence.en: She sings a beautiful song for us.

en sauna.explanation: "En sauna" means "a sauna", a hot room where you sit and sweat: Vi sidder i saunaen i ti minutter (We sit in the sauna for ten minutes). Many gyms and swimming pools have one.

sentence.da: Efter træning sidder vi i **sauna** og sveder.
sentence.en: After working out, we sit in the sauna and sweat.

en scene.explanation: "En scene" means "a stage" in a theater, and also "a scene" in a film or play: Sangeren står på scenen (The singer is standing on the stage). Scenen i filmen er sjov (The scene in the movie is funny).

sentence.da: Bandet spiller på en stor **scene** i aften.
sentence.en: The band is playing on a big stage tonight.

en scooter.explanation: "En scooter" means "a scooter" with a motor, like a small motorbike you sit on. A kick scooter that you stand on is et løbehjul: Børn elsker deres løbehjul (Kids love their kick scooters).

sentence.da: Hun kører på **scooter** gennem byen.
sentence.en: She rides a scooter through town.

en score.explanation: "En score" means "a score", the number of points in a game: Scoren er to-nul (The score is two to nothing). To score a goal, use at score: Han scorer et mål (He scores a goal).

sentence.da: Min **score** i spillet er meget høj.
sentence.en: My score in the game is very high.

en seddel.explanation: "En seddel" means "a note", a small piece of paper with writing: Jeg skriver en seddel (I write a note). It also means "a banknote": en hundredkroneseddel (a 100-krone bill).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver en **seddel** og lægger den på døren.
sentence.en: I write a note and put it on the door.

en sejlbåd.explanation: "En sejlbåd" means "a sailboat", a boat that the wind moves: Sejlbåden kommer ind i havnen (The sailboat comes into the harbor). It is built from sejl (sail) and båd (boat).

sentence.da: Når der er vind, sejler min onkel i sin **sejlbåd**.
sentence.en: When there is wind, my uncle sails in his sailboat.

en sejr.explanation: "En sejr" means "a victory", when you win: Holdet fik en stor sejr i går (The team got a big victory yesterday). The opposite is et nederlag (a defeat), and the verb is at sejre (to win).

sentence.da: Vi fejrer vores store **sejr** med kage.
sentence.en: We celebrate our big victory with cake.

en sekretær.explanation: "En sekretær" means "a secretary", someone who handles calls, mail and meetings in an office: Sekretæren booker mødet (The secretary books the meeting).

sentence.da: Vores **sekretær** svarer i telefonen.
sentence.en: Our secretary answers the phone.

en sektion.explanation: "En sektion" means "a section", a part of a larger whole: en sektion af avisen (a section of the paper). It fits a store, an office or a text.

sentence.da: Børnebøgerne står i en anden **sektion**.
sentence.en: The children's books are in another section.

en sele.explanation: "En sele" means "a seat belt" or "a harness": Tag selen på (Put your seat belt on). For a car, you can also say en sikkerhedssele (safety belt).

sentence.da: Børnene skal have **sele** på i bilen.
sentence.en: The children must wear seat belts in the car.

en seng.explanation: "En seng" means "a bed". At gå i seng means "to go to bed", with no en in it: Jeg går i seng (I am going to bed).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og går i **seng**.
sentence.en: I am tired and go to bed.

en sengegavl.explanation: "En sengegavl" means "a headboard", the board at the head end of a bed. It is senge (bed) plus gavl (end).

sentence.da: Jeg sidder i sengen og læner mig mod min **sengegavl**.
sentence.en: I sit in bed and lean against my headboard.

en serie.explanation: "En serie" means "a series", often a TV show: Hun elsker den serie (She loves that series). It also means a set of things in a row: en serie fejl (a series of mistakes).

sentence.da: Vi ser en god **serie** hver aften.
sentence.en: We watch a good series every evening.

en server.explanation: "En server" means "a server", a computer that sends data to other computers: Serveren er nede (The server is down). In a restaurant, a waiter is en tjener instead.

sentence.da: Siden virker ikke, når vores **server** er nede.
sentence.en: The site does not work when our server is down.

en service.explanation: "En service" means "a service", help given to customers: God service er vigtig i en butik (Good service is important in a store). A car also goes in for service: Bilen skal til service (The car has to go in for service). A favor is en tjeneste.

sentence.da: Vi fik rigtig god **service** på hotellet.
sentence.en: We got really good service at the hotel.

en serviet.explanation: "En serviet" means "a napkin", the cloth or paper you use at the table while eating. It is said ser-vi-ET, with the stress at the end.

sentence.da: Der ligger en **serviet** ved gaflen.
sentence.en: There is a napkin by the fork.

en seværdighed.explanation: "En seværdighed" means "an attraction", a place worth seeing. It comes from se (see) and værdig (worthy): Slottet er en seværdighed (The castle is an attraction).

sentence.da: Turisterne besøger hver **seværdighed** i byen.
sentence.en: The tourists visit every attraction in the city.

en si.explanation: "En si" means "a sieve" or "a strainer", a bowl-shaped mesh with small holes. It lets liquid or fine powder through and holds back the rest: Brug en si til melet (Use a sieve for the flour).

sentence.da: Jeg hælder te gennem en **si**.
sentence.en: I pour tea through a strainer.

en side.explanation: "En side" means "a page" or "a side", and also a web page. På side ti means "on page ten" and "på den anden side" means "on the other side". På den ene side ... på den anden side means "on the one hand ... on the other hand".

sentence.da: Åbn bogen på **side** ti.
sentence.en: Open the book on page ten.

en sikkerhedskontrol.explanation: "En sikkerhedskontrol" means "a security check", for example at an airport, where your bag goes through a scanner. It is built from sikkerhed (security) and kontrol (check).

sentence.da: Alle skal igennem en **sikkerhedskontrol** i lufthavnen.
sentence.en: Everyone has to go through a security check at the airport.

en sikkerhedskopi.explanation: "En sikkerhedskopi" means "a backup", an extra copy saved in case something is lost: Jeg laver en sikkerhedskopi af min telefon (I make a backup of my phone). It is built from sikkerhed (security) and kopi (copy).

sentence.da: Når telefonen går i stykker, har jeg en **sikkerhedskopi**.
sentence.en: When the phone breaks, I have a backup.

en sikkerhedssele.explanation: "En sikkerhedssele" means "a seatbelt". It is built from sikkerhed (safety) and sele (harness). To wear it, use have ... på: Du skal have sikkerhedsselen på (You must wear your seatbelt).

sentence.da: En **sikkerhedssele** beskytter dig i bilen.
sentence.en: A seatbelt protects you in the car.

en sikring.explanation: "En sikring" means "a fuse", the small part that cuts the power if something goes wrong: Sikringen er sprunget (The fuse has blown). It is built on at sikre (to secure).

sentence.da: Lyset gik ud, fordi en **sikring** var sprunget.
sentence.en: The light went out because a fuse had blown.

en sikringsboks.explanation: "En sikringsboks" means "a fuse box", the box with the switches that control the electricity in a home: Strømmen er gået. Tjek sikringsboksen (The power is out. Check the fuse box).

sentence.da: Lyset gik ud, og nu leder jeg efter vores **sikringsboks**.
sentence.en: The light went out and now I am looking for our fuse box.

en situation.explanation: "En situation" means "a situation", how things are at a certain moment: Vi er i en ny situation (We are in a new situation). Hvad gør du i den situation? (What do you do in that situation?)

sentence.da: Det er en svær **situation** for alle.
sentence.en: It is a hard situation for everyone.

en skade.explanation: "En skade" means "an injury" and also "damage": Han fik en skade i knæet (He got an injury to his knee). Stormen gjorde stor skade (The storm did great damage).

sentence.da: Han fik en **skade** i knæet under kampen.
sentence.en: He got an injury to his knee during the game.

en skadestue.explanation: "En skadestue" means an ER (emergency room), where you go for injuries and sudden problems. It is made of skade (injury) and stue (room). Jeg er på skadestuen means "I am at the ER", literally on the ER.

sentence.da: Læger hjælper skadede folk på en **skadestue**.
sentence.en: Doctors help injured people in an ER.

en skammel.explanation: "En skammel" means "a stool", a small seat with no back: Jeg sidder på en skammel i køkkenet (I sit on a stool in the kitchen).

sentence.da: Jeg står på en **skammel** og når hylden.
sentence.en: I stand on a stool and reach the shelf.

en skat.explanation: "En skat" means "a tax": Man betaler skat af sin løn (You pay tax on your pay). It also means "a treasure", and Danes call a loved one skat too: Hej skat (Hi, honey).

sentence.da: Vi betaler meget i **skat** i Danmark.
sentence.en: We pay a lot in tax in Denmark.

en ske.explanation: "En ske" means "a spoon". En teske (a teaspoon) and en spiseske (a tablespoon, literally an eating spoon) are built from it.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser suppen med en **ske**.
sentence.en: I eat the soup with a spoon.

en ski.explanation: "En ski" means "a ski". With more than one, the word often stays ski: Jeg har to nye ski (I have two new skis).

sentence.da: Min ene **ski** er gået i stykker.
sentence.en: One of my skis has broken.

en skildpadde.explanation: "En skildpadde" means "a turtle", and Danish uses the same word for a tortoise on land: En skildpadde går meget langsomt (A turtle walks very slowly). Its shell is en skal (a shell).

sentence.da: En **skildpadde** går langsomt, men den bliver gammel.
sentence.en: A turtle walks slowly, but it gets old.

en skilsmisse.explanation: "En skilsmisse" means "a divorce", the end of a marriage: Efter skilsmissen flyttede hun til Aarhus (After the divorce she moved to Aarhus). A person who has been through one is skilt (divorced).

sentence.da: Deres **skilsmisse** var svær for børnene.
sentence.en: Their divorce was hard on the children.

en skinke.explanation: "En skinke" means "a ham". For ham on bread or in a meal, just skinke is used, for example et stykke skinke (a piece of ham) and brød med skinke (bread with ham).

sentence.da: **Skinke** er kød fra en gris.
sentence.en: Ham is meat from a pig.

en skive.explanation: "En skive" means "a slice", for example of bread, cheese or sausage: en skive brød (a slice of bread) and to skiver ost (two slices of cheese). For a slice of cake, Danes usually say et stykke kage (a piece of cake).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer en **skive** af brødet.
sentence.en: I cut a slice off the bread.

en skjorte.explanation: "En skjorte" means "a shirt". The j in skjorte is said like an English y.

sentence.da: En **skjorte** har knapper og lange ærmer.
sentence.en: A shirt has buttons and long sleeves.

en sko.explanation: "En sko" means "a shoe". The word for more than one shoe looks the same as the single word, so you tell them apart with a number: to sko means "two shoes".

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **sko** på min fod.
sentence.en: I put a shoe on my foot.

en skobutik.explanation: "En skobutik" means "a shoe store". It is made of sko (shoes) and butik (shop).

sentence.da: Jeg køber nye sko i en **skobutik**.
sentence.en: I buy new shoes in a shoe store.

en skole.explanation: "En skole" means "a school". To say that someone is at school, Danes say i skole with no en or "the": Børnene er i skole (The children are at school).

sentence.da: Min datter går i **skole** hver dag.
sentence.en: My daughter goes to school every day.

en skoletaske.explanation: "En skoletaske" means "a school bag", the bag a child carries to school on the back. It is built from skole (school) and taske (bag).

sentence.da: Børnene har bøger og madpakke i deres **skoletaske**.
sentence.en: The kids have books and a packed lunch in their school bag.

en skoletur.explanation: "En skoletur" means "a school trip", when a class travels together for a day or longer: Vi tager på skoletur i morgen (We are going on a school trip tomorrow). It is built from en skole (a school) and en tur (a trip).

sentence.da: Hele klassen skal på **skoletur** til Berlin.
sentence.en: The whole class is going on a school trip to Berlin.

en skomager.explanation: "En skomager" means "a shoemaker" or "a cobbler", someone who makes and repairs shoes: Jeg afleverer skoene hos skomageren (I drop the shoes off at the shoemaker's). The ending -mager means a maker of something.

sentence.da: Min **skomager** kan reparere hælen på mine sko.
sentence.en: My shoemaker can fix the heel on my shoes.

en skorsten.explanation: "En skorsten" means "a chimney", the tall pipe on a roof that carries smoke away from a fireplace or stove.

sentence.da: Der kommer røg op af vores **skorsten**.
sentence.en: Smoke is coming up out of our chimney.

en skostørrelse.explanation: "En skostørrelse" means "a shoe size", the number inside your shoe. Denmark uses European sizes, so you say Jeg bruger 40 (I wear a 40).

sentence.da: Min **skostørrelse** er 40, men skoene er for små.
sentence.en: My shoe size is 40, but the shoes are too small.

en skov.explanation: "En skov" means "a forest" or "woods". A walk in the woods is en skovtur (literally a forest trip).

sentence.da: Der er mange høje træer i en **skov**.
sentence.en: There are many tall trees in a forest.

en skovl.explanation: "En skovl" means "a shovel", for lifting and moving things like sand, soil or snow: Jeg flytter sand med en skovl (I move sand with a shovel).

sentence.da: Han fjerner sneen med en **skovl**.
sentence.en: He clears the snow with a shovel.

en skovsti.explanation: "En skovsti" means "a forest path". It is built from skov (forest) and sti (path). Vi gik en tur ad skovstien (We took a walk along the forest path).

sentence.da: Vi gik langs en smal **skovsti** i går.
sentence.en: We walked along a narrow forest path yesterday.

en skraldebil.explanation: "En skraldebil" means "a garbage truck", the truck that collects trash from the bins: Skraldebilen kommer om mandagen (The garbage truck comes on Mondays).

sentence.da: Hver tirsdag kommer en **skraldebil** og henter vores skrald.
sentence.en: Every Tuesday a garbage truck comes and picks up our trash.

en skraldemand.explanation: "En skraldemand" means "a garbage collector". It is built from skrald (garbage) and mand (man): Han arbejder som skraldemand (He works as a garbage collector).

sentence.da: Vores **skraldemand** tager skraldet hver tirsdag.
sentence.en: Our garbage collector takes the garbage every Tuesday.

en skraldepose.explanation: "En skraldepose" means "a garbage bag". It is built from skrald (garbage) and en pose (a bag): Jeg tager skraldeposen med ned (I take the garbage bag down with me).

sentence.da: Jeg putter affaldet i en **skraldepose** og binder den.
sentence.en: I put the waste in a garbage bag and tie it.

en skraldespand.explanation: "En skraldespand" means "a trash can", a bin you throw garbage in, in the kitchen or on the street. It is built from skrald (garbage) and spand (bucket).

sentence.da: Jeg smider papiret i en **skraldespand**.
sentence.en: I throw the paper in a trash can.

en skrue.explanation: "En skrue" means "a screw". You turn it in with en skruetrækker (a screwdriver). Skruen sidder løst (The screw is loose).

sentence.da: Hylden falder ned, fordi der mangler en **skrue**.
sentence.en: The shelf falls down because a screw is missing.

en skruetrækker.explanation: "En skruetrækker" means "a screwdriver", the tool you hold by the handle to turn a skrue (screw) in or out. It is built from skrue (screw) and trækker (puller).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger en **skruetrækker** til at stramme skruen.
sentence.en: I use a screwdriver to tighten the screw.

en skrællekniv.explanation: "En skrællekniv" means "a paring knife", a small knife for peeling fruit and vegetables: Kan jeg låne din skrællekniv? (Can I borrow your paring knife?)

sentence.da: Jeg skræller æblet med en **skrællekniv**.
sentence.en: I peel the apple with a paring knife.

en skuespiller.explanation: "En skuespiller" means "an actor" in movies or on stage, and it is used for both men and women: Hun er en kendt skuespiller (She is a famous actor). It is built from skuespil (a play) and spiller (player).

sentence.da: Hun er **skuespiller** og arbejder på et teater.
sentence.en: She is an actor and works at a theater.

en skuffe.explanation: "En skuffe" means "a drawer", the box in a desk, dresser or kitchen unit that you slide out to reach things: Træk skuffen ud (Pull the drawer out).

sentence.da: Gaflerne ligger i en **skuffe** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: The forks are in a drawer in the kitchen.

en skuffelse.explanation: "En skuffelse" means "a disappointment": Resultatet var en skuffelse (The result was a disappointment). To say how you feel, use Jeg er skuffet (I am disappointed).

sentence.da: Det var en stor **skuffelse**, og jeg blev ked af det.
sentence.en: It was a big disappointment, and I got sad.

en skulder.explanation: "En skulder" means "a shoulder". Danish says the shoulder where English says my shoulder: Jeg har ondt i skulderen (literally I have pain in the shoulder) means "My shoulder hurts". At trække på skuldrene means "to shrug".

sentence.da: Hun lægger sin arm om min **skulder**.
sentence.en: She puts her arm around my shoulder.

en sky.explanation: "En sky" means "a cloud". There is also a different word sky that means "shy": Han er sky (He is shy). The sentence tells you which one is meant.

sentence.da: Der er en mørk **sky** på himlen.
sentence.en: There is a dark cloud in the sky.

en skygge.explanation: "En skygge" means "a shadow", and also "shade": Solen kaster en lang skygge (The sun throws a long shadow). Jeg sidder i skyggen (I am sitting in the shade).

sentence.da: Træet giver en dejlig **skygge** på varme dage.
sentence.en: The tree gives lovely shade on hot days.

en skyskraber.explanation: "En skyskraber" means "a skyscraper", a very tall building: Det er verdens højeste skyskraber (It is the world's tallest skyscraper). The word is built the same way as in English, from sky (sky) and skrabe (to scrape).

sentence.da: Fra mit hotelvindue kan jeg se en høj **skyskraber**.
sentence.en: From my hotel window I can see a tall skyscraper.

en skål.explanation: "En skål" means "a bowl". The same word, Skål!, is what you say when you raise a glass, like Cheers!.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser suppe af en **skål**.
sentence.en: I eat soup from a bowl.

en skærm.explanation: "En skærm" means "a screen", on a computer, phone or TV: Skærmen er gået sort (The screen has gone black). A cinema uses et lærred (a big canvas screen) instead.

sentence.da: Min computer har en stor **skærm**.
sentence.en: My computer has a big screen.

en skønhed.explanation: "En skønhed" means "a beauty", either the quality of being beautiful or a beautiful person or thing: Hun er en sand skønhed (She is a true beauty).

sentence.da: Jeg elsker naturens **skønhed**.
sentence.en: I love the beauty of nature.

en slags.explanation: "En slags" means "a kind of" and "a sort of". It is always en slags, even before et-words: en slags værelse (a kind of room).

sentence.da: Han bor i en **slags** hytte ved søen.
sentence.en: He lives in a kind of cabin by the lake.

en slagter.explanation: "En slagter" means "a butcher", someone who cuts up meat and sells it in a shop: Jeg køber pølser hos slagteren (I buy sausages at the butcher's).

sentence.da: Min onkel er **slagter** og sælger kød.
sentence.en: My uncle is a butcher and sells meat.

en slange.explanation: "En slange" means "a snake": Der er en slange i haven (There is a snake in the garden). The same word also means a hose: en haveslange (a garden hose).

sentence.da: En **slange** har ingen ben og kryber på jorden.
sentence.en: A snake has no legs and crawls on the ground.

en slette.explanation: "En slette" means "a plain", wide flat land with few or no hills. Be careful, at slette (to delete) looks the same: Jeg sletter filen (I delete the file).

sentence.da: Landet er en flad **slette** uden bjerge.
sentence.en: The land is a flat plain without mountains.

en slikbutik.explanation: "En slikbutik" means "a candy store", a shop that sells sweets. It is built from slik (candy) and butik (shop): Vi går forbi slikbutikken (We walk past the candy store).

sentence.da: I en **slikbutik** kan du købe slik og chokolade.
sentence.en: In a candy store you can buy candy and chocolate.

en slikpind.explanation: "En slikpind" means "a lollipop". It is built from slik (candy) and pind (stick): Jeg køber en slikpind til dig (I am buying a lollipop for you).

sentence.da: Barnet slikker på en **slikpind**.
sentence.en: The child licks a lollipop.

en slutning.explanation: "En slutning" means "an ending", for example of a film or a book: Jeg kan ikke lide slutningen (I do not like the ending). It is built from at slutte (to end).

sentence.da: Filmen har en meget sjov **slutning**.
sentence.en: The film has a very funny ending.

en slægtning.explanation: "En slægtning" means "a relative", a person in your wider family: Han er en fjern slægtning (He is a distant relative). Jeg har slægtninge i Norge (I have relatives in Norway).

sentence.da: En **slægtning** fra Norge kommer på besøg i morgen.
sentence.en: A relative from Norway is coming to visit tomorrow.

en smag.explanation: "En smag" means "a taste": Jeg kan lide smagen af citron (I like the taste of lemon). It also means a person's taste: Vi har ikke samme smag (We do not have the same taste). The action is at smage (to taste).

sentence.da: Suppen har en dejlig **smag** af hvidløg.
sentence.en: The soup has a lovely taste of garlic.

en smartphone.explanation: "En smartphone" means "a smartphone". En mobil (a mobile phone) is the shorter everyday word and can mean any mobile phone.

sentence.da: Min **smartphone** har internet og kamera.
sentence.en: My smartphone has internet and a camera.

en smerte.explanation: "En smerte" means "a pain". It is mostly used in the plural: Jeg har smerter means "I am in pain". For a pain in one place, Danes often say ondt, as in Jeg har ondt i hovedet (literally I have pain in the head, meaning "my head hurts").

sentence.da: Jeg har en skarp **smerte** i foden.
sentence.en: I have a sharp pain in my foot.

en smoothie.explanation: "En smoothie" means "a smoothie", a thick drink made of blended fruit: Jeg laver en smoothie af banan og jordbær (I make a smoothie from banana and strawberries).

sentence.da: Til morgenmad drikker jeg en **smoothie** med bær.
sentence.en: For breakfast I drink a smoothie with berries.

en sms.explanation: "En sms" means "a text message", said es-em-es. Jeg sender dig en sms (I am sending you a text). For messages in chat apps, Danes usually say en besked (a message).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver en kort **sms** til dig.
sentence.en: I write a short text message to you.

en småkage.explanation: "En småkage" means "a cookie" or "a biscuit", a small sweet treat: Vi bager småkager i dag (We are baking cookies today). It is built from små (small) and kage (cake).

sentence.da: Må jeg få en **småkage** til min te?
sentence.en: May I have a cookie with my tea?

en smørkniv.explanation: "En smørkniv" means "a butter knife", the blunt knife for spreading butter on bread: Smørkniven ligger i skuffen (The butter knife is in the drawer).

sentence.da: Giv mig en **smørkniv** til brødet.
sentence.en: Give me a butter knife for the bread.

en snack.explanation: "En snack" means "a snack". Another way to say it is en bid mad (a bite of food).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **snack** før middag.
sentence.en: I eat a snack before dinner.

en sneaker.explanation: "En sneaker" means "a sneaker", a casual shoe you can wear for sport or every day. It is mostly used in the plural: Jeg har hvide sneakers på (I am wearing white sneakers).

sentence.da: En **sneaker** er en blød sko med gummisål.
sentence.en: A sneaker is a soft shoe with a rubber sole.

en snemand.explanation: "En snemand" means "a snowman", built from sne (snow) and mand (man): Vi bygger en snemand med en gulerod som næse (We build a snowman with a carrot as a nose).

sentence.da: Børnene bygger en stor **snemand** i haven.
sentence.en: The children are building a big snowman in the garden.

en snestorm.explanation: "En snestorm" means "a snowstorm". It is built from sne (snow) and storm (storm). Togene holdt stille på grund af snestormen (The trains stood still because of the snowstorm).

sentence.da: Der kom en kraftig **snestorm** i nat.
sentence.en: A strong snowstorm came last night.

en snor.explanation: "En snor" means "a string" or "a cord", thin and light: Dragen holdes i en lang snor (The kite is held on a long string). It can also be a dog leash: Hunden skal i snor (The dog must be on a leash).

sentence.da: Hun bandt en **snor** om pakken.
sentence.en: She tied a string around the package.

en sodavand.explanation: "En sodavand" means "a soda", a fizzy soft drink such as cola or lemonade. It is built from soda (soda water) and vand (water).

sentence.da: En **sodavand** er sød og har bobler.
sentence.en: A soda is sweet and has bubbles.

en sodavandsis.explanation: "En sodavandsis" means "a popsicle", a frozen fruity ice on a stick. It is built from sodavand (soda) and is (ice): På en varm dag spiser jeg en sodavandsis (On a hot day I eat a popsicle).

sentence.da: En **sodavandsis** er frossen sodavand på en pind.
sentence.en: A popsicle is frozen soda on a stick.

en sofa.explanation: "En sofa" means "a sofa" or "a couch". The low table in front of it is et sofabord (a coffee table), built from sofa and bord (table).

sentence.da: Vi sidder på en blød **sofa**.
sentence.en: We sit on a soft sofa.

en sok.explanation: "En sok" means "a sock", something you wear on your foot, usually under a shoe. Socks come in twos, so you count them as et par sokker (a pair of socks).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **sok** på min venstre fod.
sentence.en: I have a sock on my left foot.

en sol.explanation: "En sol" means "a sun", but you mostly hear it as solen (the sun): Solen skinner means "The sun is shining". It is also part of solskin (sunshine) and solbriller (sunglasses).

sentence.da: Der er meget **sol** og varmt i dag.
sentence.en: There is a lot of sun and it is warm today.

en soldat.explanation: "En soldat" means "a soldier", a person who serves in a country's armed forces. A soldier can stand guard: Soldaten står vagt ved porten (The soldier is standing guard at the gate). The stress is on the end: sol-DAT.

sentence.da: En **soldat** har uniform på og kæmper for sit land.
sentence.en: A soldier wears a uniform and fights for his country.
