en solhat.explanation: "En solhat" means "a sun hat", a hat with a wide brim that keeps the sun off your face. It is built from sol (sun) and hat (hat): Glem ikke solhatten (Do not forget the sun hat).

sentence.da: Jeg tager min **solhat** på, når solen skinner.
sentence.en: I put on my sun hat when the sun is shining.

en solnedgang.explanation: "En solnedgang" means "a sunset": Solnedgangen er flot i aften (The sunset is beautiful tonight). It is built from sol (sun) and nedgang (going down).

sentence.da: Vi ser en **solnedgang** fra stranden.
sentence.en: We watch a sunset from the beach.

en solopgang.explanation: "En solopgang" means "a sunrise": Solopgangen er smuk over havet (The sunrise is beautiful over the sea). It is built from sol (sun) and opgang (going up).

sentence.da: Vi står tidligt op og ser en **solopgang**.
sentence.en: We get up early and watch a sunrise.

en solsikke.explanation: "En solsikke" means "a sunflower", a tall plant with a big yellow head that turns toward the light: Solsikkerne står langs vejen (The sunflowers stand along the road). It starts with sol (sun).

sentence.da: Den høje **solsikke** vender sig mod solen.
sentence.en: The tall sunflower turns toward the sun.

en solsort.explanation: "En solsort" means "a blackbird", a common garden bird with a lovely song: Solsorten synger i haven (The blackbird sings in the garden). The male is black with a yellow beak.

sentence.da: En **solsort** synger i træet foran huset.
sentence.en: A blackbird sings in the tree in front of the house.

en sommer.explanation: "En sommer" means "a summer", the warm season after spring and before autumn. To say in the summer, use om sommeren: Om sommeren er det lyst længe (In the summer it stays light late).

sentence.da: I **sommer** bader vi i havet.
sentence.en: This summer we swim in the sea.

en sommerdag.explanation: "En sommerdag" means "a summer day". It is built from sommer (summer) and dag (day): Hun elsker en lang sommerdag ved stranden (She loves a long summer day at the beach).

sentence.da: Det er en varm **sommerdag**, og vi svømmer i havet.
sentence.en: It is a warm summer day, and we are swimming in the sea.

en sommerferie.explanation: "En sommerferie" means "a summer vacation". It is built from sommer (summer) and ferie (vacation), and you say i sommerferien (during the summer vacation).

sentence.da: I vores **sommerferie** bader vi i havet.
sentence.en: During our summer vacation we swim in the sea.

en sommerfest.explanation: "En sommerfest" means "a summer party", a party held in the warm months, often outside: Børnene glæder sig til sommerfesten (The children look forward to the summer party).

sentence.da: Vi holder **sommerfest** i haven, når det er varmt.
sentence.en: We are having a summer party in the garden when it is warm.

en sommerfugl.explanation: "En sommerfugl" means "a butterfly", an insect with colorful wings that you mostly see in warm weather. It is built from sommer (summer) and fugl (bird), so it is literally a summer bird.

sentence.da: En **sommerfugl** har store vinger og flyver fra blomst til blomst.
sentence.en: A butterfly has big wings and flies from flower to flower.

en sommerkjole.explanation: "En sommerkjole" means "a summer dress", a light dress for warm days. It is built from sommer (summer) and kjole (dress): Jeg har en blå sommerkjole (I have a blue summer dress).

sentence.da: Hun har en gul **sommerkjole** på til festen.
sentence.en: She is wearing a yellow summer dress to the party.

en sommernat.explanation: "En sommernat" means "a summer night". It is built from sommer (summer) and nat (night): Vi sad ude hele sommernatten (We sat outside the whole summer night).

sentence.da: Vi sover med åbent vindue på en varm **sommernat**.
sentence.en: We sleep with the window open on a warm summer night.

en sosu-assistent.explanation: "En sosu-assistent" means "a health care assistant", someone who helps sick or older people with daily care: Hun er sosu-assistent (She is a health care assistant).

sentence.da: Min mor arbejder som **sosu-assistent** på et plejehjem.
sentence.en: My mother works as a health care assistant at a nursing home.

en souvenir.explanation: "En souvenir" means "a souvenir", a small thing you bring home from a trip: Hun køber en souvenir i hver by (She buys a souvenir in every city). Souvenirs are often sold in a turistbutik (tourist shop).

sentence.da: Jeg købte en lille **souvenir** til min mor.
sentence.en: I bought a small souvenir for my mother.

en sovepose.explanation: "En sovepose" means "a sleeping bag". It is built from sove (to sleep) and pose (bag): Jeg tager min sovepose med (I am bringing my sleeping bag).

sentence.da: Jeg fryser ikke, fordi min **sovepose** er varm.
sentence.en: I am not cold because my sleeping bag is warm.

en sovesofa.explanation: "En sovesofa" means "a sofa bed", a sofa that folds out into a bed. It is built from sove (to sleep) and sofa (sofa).

sentence.da: Gæsterne kan sove i vores **sovesofa**.
sentence.en: The guests can sleep in our sofa bed.

en sovs.explanation: "En sovs" means "a sauce" or "gravy". Tomatsovs (tomato sauce) is built on it. The spelling en sauce (a sauce) is also used.

sentence.da: Frikadellerne smager godt med brun **sovs**.
sentence.en: The meatballs taste good with brown gravy.

en spand.explanation: "En spand" means "a bucket", for water, sand or cleaning: Hent en spand vand (Get a bucket of water). You do not need af (of) between the two words.

sentence.da: Jeg fylder en **spand** med varmt vand.
sentence.en: I fill a bucket with hot water.

en spanier.explanation: "En spanier" means "a Spaniard", a person from Spain. For things from Spain, use spansk instead: spansk vin (Spanish wine) and spansk mad (Spanish food).

sentence.da: Han er **spanier**, men han bor i Danmark nu.
sentence.en: He is Spanish, but he lives in Denmark now.

en speeder.explanation: "En speeder" means "an accelerator", the pedal you press to go faster: Han trådte hårdt på speederen (He stepped hard on the accelerator). The pedal you use to slow down is en bremse (a brake).

sentence.da: En **speeder** får bilen til at køre hurtigere.
sentence.en: An accelerator makes the car go faster.

en spids.explanation: "En spids" means "a tip" or "a point", the narrow end of something: spidsen af næsen (the tip of the nose). It can also be spids (pointed), like en spids kniv (a pointed knife).

sentence.da: Min blyant har en brækket **spids**.
sentence.en: My pencil has a broken tip.

en spiller.explanation: "En spiller" means "a player" in a game or sport: Hun er klubbens bedste spiller (She is the club's best player). It also works for music: en guitarspiller (a guitar player).

sentence.da: En **spiller** løber efter bolden på banen.
sentence.en: A player runs after the ball on the field.

en spion.explanation: "En spion" means "a spy", someone who secretly gets information for another country or company: Han var spion under krigen (He was a spy during the war). The action is at spionere (to spy).

sentence.da: En **spion** arbejder i hemmelighed for et andet land.
sentence.en: A spy works in secret for another country.

en spiral.explanation: "En spiral" means "a spiral", a shape that winds round and round: en spiral af røg (a spiral of smoke).

sentence.da: Trappen snor sig op i en **spiral**.
sentence.en: The stairs wind up in a spiral.

en spiseske.explanation: "En spiseske" means "a tablespoon", the big spoon used for measuring in recipes: Tilsæt en spiseske mel (Add a tablespoon of flour). It is built from at spise (to eat) and ske (spoon).

sentence.da: Opskriften kræver en **spiseske** smør.
sentence.en: The recipe requires a tablespoon of butter.

en spisestue.explanation: "En spisestue" means "a dining room", the room with the dining table. It is built from spise (to eat) and stue (living room): Vi spiser i spisestuen, når vi har gæster (We eat in the dining room when we have guests).

sentence.da: Vi spiser aftensmad i en stor **spisestue**.
sentence.en: We eat dinner in a big dining room.

en spisning.explanation: "En spisning" means "a shared meal", an event that people organize together, for example for a club. For an ordinary meal, say et måltid (a meal).

sentence.da: Vi laver mad sammen til klubbens **spisning**.
sentence.en: We cook together for the club's shared meal.

en sportsklub.explanation: "En sportsklub" means "a sports club", a group where people train and play together: Jeg er med i en sportsklub (I am in a sports club). It is built from sport (sport) and klub (club).

sentence.da: Jeg træner to gange om ugen i min **sportsklub**.
sentence.en: I work out twice a week at my sports club.

en sportstaske.explanation: "En sportstaske" means "a gym bag", a bag for your sports clothes and shoes: Min sportstaske er tung (My gym bag is heavy). It is built from sport (sport) and taske (bag).

sentence.da: Jeg pakker tøj og sko i min **sportstaske**.
sentence.en: I pack clothes and shoes in my gym bag.

en sporvogn.explanation: "En sporvogn" means "a tram", an electric car that runs on rails in the street. It is built from spor (track) and vogn (car): Sporvognen holder midt på gaden (The tram stops in the middle of the street).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **sporvogn** gennem den gamle by.
sentence.en: We take a tram through the old town.

en sprogskole.explanation: "En sprogskole" means "a language school", a school where adults learn a new language: Jeg går på sprogskole to gange om ugen (I go to language school twice a week).

sentence.da: Jeg lærer dansk på en **sprogskole** i byen.
sentence.en: I am learning Danish at a language school in town.

en spøg.explanation: "En spøg" means "a joke" or "a prank", something said or done for fun and not meant seriously. For a joke with a punchline, Danes often say en vits (a joke) instead.

sentence.da: Det var kun en **spøg**, og alle grinede.
sentence.en: It was only a joke, and everyone laughed.

en squash.explanation: "En squash" means "a zucchini". The sport has the same name but no en: Han spiller squash (He plays squash). Jeg steger en squash (I fry a zucchini).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer en **squash** i tynde skiver.
sentence.en: I cut a zucchini into thin slices.

en squat.explanation: "En squat" means "a squat", the exercise where you bend your knees and go down, then stand up again: Jeg tager ti squats (I do ten squats).

sentence.da: Jeg bøjer knæene i en dyb **squat**.
sentence.en: I bend my knees in a deep squat.

en stak.explanation: "En stak" means "a stack", things placed neatly on top of each other: en stak tallerkener (a stack of plates). A messy one is en bunke (a pile).

sentence.da: Der ligger en høj **stak** bøger på bordet.
sentence.en: There is a tall stack of books on the table.

en stald.explanation: "En stald" means "a stable", the building where farm animals sleep and stay warm: Dyrene sover i stalden (The animals sleep in the stable). It is not only for horses; it is used for cows and pigs too.

sentence.da: Vi har en stor **stald** til hestene.
sentence.en: We have a big stable for the horses.

en stank.explanation: "En stank" means "a stench", a very bad smell: Der var en stank af fisk (There was a stench of fish). A neutral smell is en lugt (a smell), and a nice one is en duft (a scent).

sentence.da: Der er en forfærdelig **stank** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: There is a terrible stench in the kitchen.

en station.explanation: "En station" means "a station", a place where trains, metros or buses stop. På stationen means "at the station". For a train station only, say en togstation (a train station).

sentence.da: Vi venter på toget på en **station**.
sentence.en: We wait for the train at a station.

en statsminister.explanation: "En statsminister" means "a prime minister", the head of a government. It is built from stat (state) and minister (minister): Statsministeren taler i aften (The prime minister speaks tonight).

sentence.da: Danmarks **statsminister** leder landets regering.
sentence.en: Denmark's prime minister leads the country's government.

en statue.explanation: "En statue" means "a statue", a figure of a person or an animal made of stone or metal: Statuen er lavet af bronze (The statue is made of bronze).

sentence.da: Der står en gammel **statue** af en konge.
sentence.en: There is an old statue of a king.

en status.explanation: "En status" means "a status", how things stand right now: Hvad er status på projektet? (What is the status of the project?) Vi laver en status hver fredag (We do a status update every Friday).

sentence.da: Chefen vil have en **status** på arbejdet i dag.
sentence.en: The boss wants a status update on the work today.

en stedfar.explanation: "En stedfar" means "a stepfather", your mother's husband when he is not your birth father: Min stedfar har to børn (My stepfather has two children). It is built from sted- (step) and far (father).

sentence.da: Min mor er gift med min **stedfar**, ikke min far.
sentence.en: My mother is married to my stepfather, not my father.

en stedmor.explanation: "En stedmor" means "a stepmother", your father's wife when she is not your birth mother: Min stedmor er rigtig sød (My stepmother is really nice). It is built from sted- (step) and mor (mother).

sentence.da: Min far er gift med min **stedmor**, ikke min mor.
sentence.en: My father is married to my stepmother, not my mother.

en stegepande.explanation: "En stegepande" means "a frying pan". It is stege (to fry) and pande (pan) joined into one word. You can also say just en pande (a pan).

sentence.da: Jeg steger æg på en varm **stegepande**.
sentence.en: I fry eggs in a hot frying pan.

en stemme.explanation: "En stemme" means "a voice" and also "a vote": Hun har en smuk stemme (She has a beautiful voice). Hver stemme tæller (Every vote counts).

sentence.da: Hendes **stemme** er blød og rolig.
sentence.en: Her voice is soft and calm.

en stemning.explanation: "En stemning" means "a mood" or "an atmosphere", the feeling in a room or group: Der var god stemning til festen (The mood at the party was good). It is about the whole place, not one person.

sentence.da: Der er en rar **stemning** i klassen.
sentence.en: There is a nice atmosphere in the class.

en sten.explanation: "En sten" means "a stone" or "a rock". The plural sten looks the same as the singular, so mange sten means "many stones". As a material, it is used alone, with no en.

sentence.da: Muren er lavet af **sten**.
sentence.en: The wall is made of stone.

en stewardesse.explanation: "En stewardesse" means "a flight attendant", a woman who helps passengers on a plane. A man is en steward (a male flight attendant).

sentence.da: Hun arbejder som **stewardesse** og rejser meget.
sentence.en: She works as a flight attendant and travels a lot.

en sti.explanation: "En sti" means "a path", a narrow way for walking in a forest or field, with no cars: Vi går på stien (We are walking on the path).

sentence.da: Den lille **sti** går gennem skoven og ned til søen.
sentence.en: The little path goes through the forest and down to the lake.

en stige.explanation: "En stige" means "a ladder". It looks like the verb at stige (to rise or go up): Prisen stiger (The price is going up).

sentence.da: Han står på en **stige** og skifter pæren.
sentence.en: He is standing on a ladder and changing the bulb.

en stikdåse.explanation: "En stikdåse" means "a power strip", one plug that gives you several outlets, so many devices can share one wall outlet.

sentence.da: Jeg kan sætte fem ting i den nye **stikdåse**.
sentence.en: I can plug five things into the new power strip.

en stikkontakt.explanation: "En stikkontakt" means "an outlet" in the wall, where you plug things in: Der er en stikkontakt ved sengen (There is an outlet by the bed). The plug itself is et stik.

sentence.da: Jeg sætter min oplader i en **stikkontakt**.
sentence.en: I put my charger in an outlet.

en stil.explanation: "En stil" means "a style", the way someone dresses or does things: Hun har sin egen stil (She has her own style).

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide din **stil**, især dine sko.
sentence.en: I like your style, especially your shoes.

en stilling.explanation: "En stilling" means "a position", especially a job: Hun søger en stilling som lærer (She is applying for a job as a teacher). In sports, it is the score: Stillingen er 2-1 (The score is 2-1).

sentence.da: Hun har fået en ny **stilling** i Aarhus.
sentence.en: She has gotten a new job in Aarhus.

en stjerne.explanation: "En stjerne" means "a star", either in the sky or as a rating. A hotel with fem stjerner has five stars.

sentence.da: Om natten ser vi en **stjerne** på himlen.
sentence.en: At night we see a star in the sky.

en stol.explanation: "En stol" means "a chair". In Danish, you sit på (on) a chair: Sæt dig på stolen (Sit down on the chair).

sentence.da: Jeg sidder på en **stol** ved bordet.
sentence.en: I am sitting on a chair at the table.

en storby.explanation: "En storby" means "a big city", a large city with many people: København er en storby (Copenhagen is a big city). It is the opposite of en landsby (a village).

sentence.da: Jeg vil bo i en **storby**, fordi der sker meget.
sentence.en: I want to live in a big city because a lot happens there.

en storebror.explanation: "En storebror" means "a big brother": any brother who is older than you, whatever the age gap.

sentence.da: Min **storebror** er ti år ældre end mig.
sentence.en: My big brother is ten years older than me.

en storesøster.explanation: "En storesøster" means "a big sister": any sister who is older than you, whatever the age gap.

sentence.da: Min **storesøster** er tre år ældre end mig.
sentence.en: My big sister is three years older than me.

en storm.explanation: "En storm" means "a storm" with very strong wind. It is stronger than blæst (windy weather) and weaker than en orkan (a hurricane).

sentence.da: Der kommer en **storm** med meget vind.
sentence.en: A storm is coming with a lot of wind.

en straf.explanation: "En straf" means "a punishment": Det er en hård straf (That is a harsh punishment). You get it with at få en straf (to get a punishment), and you give it with at give en straf (to give a punishment).

sentence.da: Børn får en **straf**, når de gør noget forkert.
sentence.en: Children get a punishment when they do something wrong.

en strand.explanation: "En strand" means "a beach", the sandy edge of the sea or a lake. You say på stranden (at the beach), using på (on), not i (in).

sentence.da: Der er sand og hav ved en **strand**.
sentence.en: There is sand and sea at a beach.

en strandpromenade.explanation: "En strandpromenade" means "a beach promenade", a wide path for walking along the beach: Vi går en tur på strandpromenaden (We take a walk on the beach promenade).

sentence.da: Vi går langs havet på en lang **strandpromenade**.
sentence.en: We walk along the sea on a long beach promenade.

en strandtur.explanation: "En strandtur" means "a trip to the beach", usually a short outing for the day: Vi tager på strandtur (We are going on a trip to the beach). It is built from strand (beach) and tur (trip).

sentence.da: Vi tager på **strandtur**, hvis det bliver pænt vejr.
sentence.en: We are going on a trip to the beach if the weather is nice.

en streamingtjeneste.explanation: "En streamingtjeneste" means "a streaming service", built from streaming (streaming) and en tjeneste (a service): Netflix er en streamingtjeneste (Netflix is a streaming service).

sentence.da: Vi betaler for en **streamingtjeneste** hver måned.
sentence.en: We pay for a streaming service every month.

en streg.explanation: "En streg" means "a line" or "a stroke" drawn with a pen: Tegn en streg (Draw a line). It is also a stripe on clothes: en trøje med streger (a shirt with stripes).

sentence.da: Tegn en **streg** på papiret med en lineal.
sentence.en: Draw a line on the paper with a ruler.

en strømpe.explanation: "En strømpe" means "a stocking" or "a sock", a soft piece of clothing that covers your foot. You wear strømper inside your shoes: Jeg har strømper på (I am wearing socks).

sentence.da: Man har en **strømpe** på hver fod.
sentence.en: You wear a sock on each foot.

en studerende.explanation: "En studerende" means "a student", especially at a university: Der er mange studerende i byen (There are many students in town). The plural is studerende too. For a school child, use en elev (a pupil).

sentence.da: Hun er **studerende** på universitetet.
sentence.en: She is a student at the university.

en stue.explanation: "En stue" means "a living room", the room where you sit, relax and have guests. It also gives the ground floor its name: stueetagen (the ground floor).

sentence.da: Vi har en sofa i vores **stue**.
sentence.en: We have a sofa in our living room.

en styrke.explanation: "En styrke" means "a strength", a thing you are good at: Min styrke er at lytte (My strength is listening). It also means physical power: Han har stor styrke i armene (He has great strength in his arms).

sentence.da: Matematik er min **styrke**, men sprog er svært.
sentence.en: Math is my strength, but languages are hard.

en størrelse.explanation: "En størrelse" means "a size", for clothes, shoes or anything else. It comes from stor (big), so en større størrelse is a bigger size.

sentence.da: Har I en større **størrelse** i kjolen?
sentence.en: Do you have a bigger size in the dress?

en støtte.explanation: "En støtte" means "a support", help or something that holds you up: Tak for din støtte (Thank you for your support). It can be money too: en støtte fra staten (support from the state).

sentence.da: Min familie er en stor **støtte**.
sentence.en: My family is a great support.

en støvle.explanation: "En støvle" means "a boot". Boots come in pairs, so you often hear et par støvler (a pair of boots). Rubber boots are gummistøvler, built on the same word.

sentence.da: Min venstre **støvle** er våd i regnen.
sentence.en: My left boot is wet in the rain.

en støvsuger.explanation: "En støvsuger" means "a vacuum cleaner". It is built from støv (dust) and suger (sucker): Jeg bruger støvsugeren hver lørdag (I use the vacuum cleaner every Saturday).

sentence.da: Jeg henter en **støvsuger** og gør stuen ren.
sentence.en: I get a vacuum cleaner and clean the living room.

en succes.explanation: "En succes" means "a success", something that went well: Festen blev en succes (The party was a success). Without en, it means success in general: Han har succes som forfatter (He is successful as an author).

sentence.da: Middagen blev en stor **succes**.
sentence.en: The dinner was a big success.

en suite.explanation: "En suite" means "a suite", a large, fine hotel room, often with a separate living area: Vi har booket en suite (We have booked a suite).

sentence.da: Vi har booket en **suite** med to soveværelser.
sentence.en: We have booked a suite with two bedrooms.

en sukkerskål.explanation: "En sukkerskål" means "a sugar bowl", the small bowl for sugar on the table: Kan du række mig sukkerskålen? (Can you pass me the sugar bowl?)

sentence.da: Sukkeret ligger i en lille **sukkerskål**.
sentence.en: The sugar is in a small sugar bowl.

en sum.explanation: "En sum" means "a sum", an amount of money or the result of adding numbers. In math, summen af to og tre er fem (the sum of two and three is five).

sentence.da: Han betalte en stor **sum** for huset.
sentence.en: He paid a large sum for the house.

en sundhedsplejerske.explanation: "En sundhedsplejerske" means "a health visitor", built from sundhed (health) and pleje (care). She is a nurse who checks on babies and small children: Sundhedsplejersken kommer på besøg (The health visitor comes for a visit).

sentence.da: Vi har en tid hos en **sundhedsplejerske** med babyen.
sentence.en: We have an appointment with a health visitor for the baby.

en suppe.explanation: "En suppe" means "a soup", as in tomatsuppe (tomato soup). The verb to use is at spise (to eat), not at drikke (to drink).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en varm **suppe** med en ske.
sentence.en: I eat hot soup with a spoon.

en sut.explanation: "En sut" means "a pacifier", the rubber tip a baby sucks on: Barnet græder uden sin sut (The child cries without its pacifier). Hvor er suden? (Where is the pacifier?).

sentence.da: Babyen falder i søvn med sin **sut** i munden.
sentence.en: The baby falls asleep with its pacifier in its mouth.

en sutteflaske.explanation: "En sutteflaske" means "a baby bottle", the bottle a baby drinks milk from: Har du husket sutteflasken? (Did you remember the baby bottle?). Jeg varmer en sutteflaske (I warm up a baby bottle).

sentence.da: Babyen drikker mælk af en **sutteflaske**.
sentence.en: The baby drinks milk from a baby bottle.

en svamp.explanation: "En svamp" means "a mushroom", and also "a sponge" for washing: Jeg samler svampe om efteråret (I pick mushrooms in the fall). Jeg vasker op med en svamp (I wash up with a sponge).

sentence.da: Han fandt en stor **svamp** i skoven.
sentence.en: He found a big mushroom in the forest.

en svane.explanation: "En svane" means "a swan", a large white water bird with a long neck: Svanerne svømmer på søen (The swans swim on the lake). A baby swan is en svaneunge (a cygnet).

sentence.da: En hvid **svane** svømmer på søen.
sentence.en: A white swan swims on the lake.

en svensker.explanation: "En svensker" means "a Swede", a person from Sweden: Min kollega er svensker (My colleague is Swedish). The country is Sverige, and the language is svensk (Swedish).

sentence.da: Han er **svensker** og kommer fra Malmø.
sentence.en: He is Swedish and comes from Malmö.

en svigerdatter.explanation: "En svigerdatter" means "a daughter-in-law", your son's wife: Min svigerdatter er meget sød (My daughter-in-law is very sweet).

sentence.da: Min søns kone er min **svigerdatter**.
sentence.en: My son's wife is my daughter-in-law.

en svigerfar.explanation: "En svigerfar" means "a father-in-law", the father of your husband or wife: Min svigerfar elsker at fiske (My father-in-law loves to fish). It is built from sviger- (in-law) and far (father).

sentence.da: Min **svigerfar** er pensioneret.
sentence.en: My father-in-law is retired.

en svigerinde.explanation: "En svigerinde" means "a sister-in-law", your brother's wife or your spouse's sister: Min svigerinde bor i København (My sister-in-law lives in Copenhagen).

sentence.da: Min **svigerinde** er gift med min bror.
sentence.en: My sister-in-law is married to my brother.

en svigermor.explanation: "En svigermor" means "a mother-in-law", the mother of your husband or wife: Min svigermor bager gode boller (My mother-in-law bakes good buns). It is built from sviger- (in-law) and mor (mother).

sentence.da: Min **svigermor** kommer til middag i aften.
sentence.en: My mother-in-law is coming to dinner tonight.

en svigersøn.explanation: "En svigersøn" means "a son-in-law", your daughter's husband: Min svigersøn er meget flink (My son-in-law is very nice).

sentence.da: Min datters mand er min **svigersøn**.
sentence.en: My daughter's husband is my son-in-law.

en svinestald.explanation: "En svinestald" means "a pigsty", the building where pigs live on a farm. It is built from svin (pig) and stald (stable): Der lugter i svinestalden (It smells in the pigsty).

sentence.da: Grisene bor i en varm **svinestald** på gården.
sentence.en: The pigs live in a warm pigsty on the farm.

en svoger.explanation: "En svoger" means "a brother-in-law", your sister's husband or your spouse's brother: Min svoger arbejder som tømrer (My brother-in-law works as a carpenter).

sentence.da: Min **svoger** er gift med min søster.
sentence.en: My brother-in-law is married to my sister.

en svømmehal.explanation: "En svømmehal" means "an indoor swimming pool", a public building where you can swim all year: Vi går i svømmehallen i dag (We are going to the swimming pool today). It is built from at svømme (to swim) and en hal (a hall).

sentence.da: Vi går i **svømmehal** hver lørdag, og børnene elsker det.
sentence.en: We go to the swimming pool every Saturday, and the children love it.

en svømmetur.explanation: "En svømmetur" means "a swim", a trip to swim for fun or exercise: Vi tager en svømmetur i søen (We go for a swim in the lake). It is built from svømme (to swim) and tur (trip).

sentence.da: Efter arbejde tager jeg en **svømmetur** i poolen.
sentence.en: After work I go for a swim in the pool.

en sweater.explanation: "En sweater" means "a sweater", a warm top you pull over your head. To say you are wearing one, use have ... på (literally have ... on): Jeg har en sweater på (I am wearing a sweater).

sentence.da: Du kan holde varmen i en **sweater**.
sentence.en: You can stay warm in a sweater.

en sygdom.explanation: "En sygdom" means "a disease" or "an illness". It comes from syg (sick). You say Jeg er syg (I am sick) about yourself, and "en sygdom" for the illness itself.

sentence.da: Han er syg og har en alvorlig **sygdom**.
sentence.en: He is sick and has a serious illness.

en sygeplejerske.explanation: "En sygeplejerske" means "a nurse". It comes from sygepleje (nursing). Male nurses are also called "sygeplejerske" in Danish, so the word is not only for women.

sentence.da: Min søster er **sygeplejerske** på et hospital.
sentence.en: My sister is a nurse at a hospital.

en sæk.explanation: "En sæk" means "a sack", a big bag of cloth or paper that holds heavy things like potatoes or flour. A small shopping bag is not a sæk.

sentence.da: Kartoflerne ligger i en **sæk** i kælderen.
sentence.en: The potatoes are in a sack in the cellar.

en sæl.explanation: "En sæl" means "a seal", the animal that swims in the sea and rests on rocks: Sælen ligger på en sten (The seal is lying on a rock). A seal on a document is a different word: et segl (a stamp seal).

sentence.da: En **sæl** fanger fisk i havet.
sentence.en: A seal catches fish in the sea.

en sælger.explanation: "En sælger" means "a salesperson", someone who sells things for a living: Sælgeren viste os en ny telefon (The salesperson showed us a new phone). It comes from at sælge (to sell).

sentence.da: En **sælger** hjælper kunderne i butikken.
sentence.en: A salesperson helps the customers in the store.

en sælgerske.explanation: "En sælgerske" means "a saleswoman". The word sounds old-fashioned today, and people usually say en sælger (a salesperson) for both men and women: Sælgeren hjalp mig (The salesperson helped me).

sentence.da: Den venlige **sælgerske** hjalp mig med skoene.
sentence.en: The friendly saleswoman helped me with the shoes.

en sæson.explanation: "En sæson" means "a season" for sports, TV shows and fruit: Jordbærsæsonen starter i juni (The strawberry season starts in June). For spring, summer, fall and winter, use en årstid.

sentence.da: Tv-serien har ti afsnit i hver **sæson**.
sentence.en: The TV series has ten episodes in each season.

en sætning.explanation: "En sætning" means "a sentence", words that make a full thought: Skriv en sætning (Write a sentence). For a prison sentence, use en dom (a verdict) or en straf (a punishment) instead.

sentence.da: En **sætning** slutter med et punktum.
sentence.en: A sentence ends with a period.

en sø.explanation: "En sø" means "a lake", a body of fresh water with land all around it. Do not mix it up with et hav (a sea), which is much bigger and salty.

sentence.da: Man kan bade og fiske i en **sø**.
sentence.en: You can swim and fish in a lake.

en søgemaskine.explanation: "En søgemaskine" means "a search engine", a website where you look for things online: Google er en søgemaskine (Google is a search engine). Jeg finder svaret med en søgemaskine (I find the answer with a search engine).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger ofte en **søgemaskine** til at finde opskrifter.
sentence.en: I often use a search engine to find recipes.

en søn.explanation: "En søn" means "a son". It is used for a son of any age, even a grown-up one: Hendes søn er tredive (Her son is thirty).

sentence.da: Min bror har en **søn** og en datter.
sentence.en: My brother has a son and a daughter.

en søster.explanation: "En søster" means "a sister". For a sister who shares only one parent, say en halvsøster (a half sister).

sentence.da: Min **søster** og jeg har samme mor.
sentence.en: My sister and I have the same mother.

et s-tog.explanation: "Et S-tog" means "an S-train", the commuter train around Copenhagen: Der kommer et S-tog hvert tiende minut (An S-train comes every ten minutes). It stops at many small stations.

sentence.da: Jeg tager et **S-tog** ind til byen.
sentence.en: I take an S-train into the city.

et salg.explanation: "Et salg" means "a sale", the act of selling something: Salget af huset gik godt (The sale of the house went well). For a discount sale, use et udsalg (a clearance sale).

sentence.da: Han tjener penge på **salg** af brugte biler.
sentence.en: He makes money from the sale of used cars.

et samarbejde.explanation: "Et samarbejde" means "a collaboration", people or groups working together toward the same goal. It is built from sammen (together) and arbejde (work).

sentence.da: Vi har et godt **samarbejde** med skolen.
sentence.en: We have a good collaboration with the school.

et samfund.explanation: "Et samfund" means "a society", the whole community of people in a country. Det danske samfund er trygt (Danish society is safe). Et samfund har både regler og traditioner (A society has both rules and traditions).

sentence.da: Hvert **samfund** har sine egne regler.
sentence.en: Every society has its own rules.

et samtaleemne.explanation: "Et samtaleemne" means "a topic of conversation", built from samtale (conversation) and emne (topic): Fodbold er et godt samtaleemne (Soccer is a good topic of conversation).

sentence.da: Vejret er altid et godt **samtaleemne**.
sentence.en: The weather is always a good topic of conversation.

et sekund.explanation: "Et sekund" means "a second". Do not mix it up with second meaning number two: that is anden. Et øjeblik (a moment) is a similar short wait: Et øjeblik, tak (One moment, please).

sentence.da: Det tager kun et **sekund**.
sentence.en: It only takes a second.

et selskab.explanation: "Et selskab" means "a company" in business, and also "a party" or "a social gathering": Vi var til et selskab hos naboerne (We were at a party at the neighbors'). For a business only, firma (company) is also common.

sentence.da: Vi holder et **selskab** for vores venner i morgen.
sentence.en: We are throwing a party for our friends tomorrow.

et semester.explanation: "Et semester" means "a semester", half of a school year at a school or university: Mit første semester starter i september (My first semester starts in September).

sentence.da: Vi har eksamen i slutningen af hvert **semester**.
sentence.en: We have exams at the end of each semester.

et shot.explanation: "Et shot" means "a shot", a small strong drink or a small amount of coffee: et shot espresso (a shot of espresso), et shot vodka (a shot of vodka).

sentence.da: Jeg tager et **shot** espresso om morgenen.
sentence.en: I have a shot of espresso in the morning.

et show.explanation: "Et show" means "a show", a live performance with music, dance or comedy: Showet starter klokken otte (The show starts at eight).

sentence.da: Vi så et fedt **show** med sang og dans i går.
sentence.en: We saw a cool show with singing and dancing yesterday.

et skab.explanation: "Et skab" means "a cupboard", and also a cabinet, a closet or a locker: any closed space for storing things. Words are added to say which kind, for example et køleskab (a refrigerator, literally a cooling cupboard).

sentence.da: Tallerkenerne står i et **skab**.
sentence.en: The plates are in a cupboard.

et skema.explanation: "Et skema" means "a schedule", such as the list of lessons for the week: Hvad står der på skemaet i dag? (What is on the schedule today?) It can also mean a form to fill in: Udfyld skemaet (Fill in the form).

sentence.da: Der er gymnastik på mit **skema** hver torsdag.
sentence.en: There is gym on my schedule every Thursday.

et skib.explanation: "Et skib" means "a ship". A smaller boat is en båd (a boat), and a cruise ship is et krydstogtskib (a cruise ship).

sentence.da: Et stort **skib** sejler over havet til Norge.
sentence.en: A big ship sails across the sea to Norway.

et skift.explanation: "Et skift" means "a change": et skift i planen (a change in the plan). It also means "a work shift", like a day or night shift: et natskift (a night shift).

sentence.da: Han tager et ekstra **skift** i morgen.
sentence.en: He is taking an extra shift tomorrow.

et skilt.explanation: "Et skilt" means "a sign", a board with words or a picture: Der er et skilt ved vejen (There is a sign by the road). Watch out: Hun er skilt (She is divorced) uses the same word in another way.

sentence.da: Et **skilt** viser vej til stationen.
sentence.en: A sign shows the way to the station.

et skohorn.explanation: "Et skohorn" means "a shoehorn", a curved piece that helps your heel slide into a shoe. The name is sko (shoe) plus horn (horn): Min far bruger altid skohornet (My dad always uses the shoehorn).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **skohorn**, fordi skoene er stramme.
sentence.en: I use a shoehorn because the shoes are tight.

et skolefag.explanation: "Et skolefag" means "a school subject", like math, history or English: Matematik er et vigtigt skolefag (Math is an important school subject). It is built from en skole (a school) and et fag (a subject).

sentence.da: Hvilket **skolefag** kan du bedst lide?
sentence.en: Which school subject do you like best?

et skoleår.explanation: "Et skoleår" means "a school year", from the end of one summer vacation to the next: Vi har prøve i slutningen af skoleåret (We have a test at the end of the school year).

sentence.da: Efter sommerferien begynder et nyt **skoleår**.
sentence.en: After the summer vacation a new school year begins.

et skridt.explanation: "Et skridt" means "a step", one movement of the foot: Tag et skridt tilbage (Take a step back). It can also be a move in a plan: første skridt (first step). A step on a stairway is et trin (a step).

sentence.da: Hun tog et **skridt** frem og smilede.
sentence.en: She took a step forward and smiled.

et skrig.explanation: "Et skrig" means "a scream", a loud cry from fear or pain: Barnet gav et højt skrig (The child let out a loud scream). A quiet sound is the opposite: en hvisken (a whisper).

sentence.da: Vi hørte et **skrig** fra gaden.
sentence.en: We heard a scream from the street.

et skrivebord.explanation: "Et skrivebord" means "a desk". It is built from skrive (write) and bord (table): Min computer står på skrivebordet (My computer is on the desk).

sentence.da: Hun sidder ved sit **skrivebord** og arbejder.
sentence.en: She sits at her desk and works.

et skud.explanation: "Et skud" means "a shot", from a gun or a kick in sports: Han tog et skud på mål (He took a shot on goal). For a small strong drink, use et shot (a shot).

sentence.da: Vi hørte et højt **skud** i skoven.
sentence.en: We heard a loud shot in the forest.

et skur.explanation: "Et skur" means "a shed", a small building for tools, bikes or wood: Cyklen står i skuret (The bike is in the shed). It can also mean a rain shower, as in et regnskur (a rain shower).

sentence.da: Vi har et lille **skur** bag huset.
sentence.en: We have a small shed behind the house.

et skæg.explanation: "Et skæg" means "a beard". En mand med skæg means "a man with a beard". A mustache is et overskæg, literally an over-beard.

sentence.da: Min far har et langt **skæg**.
sentence.en: My father has a long beard.

et skærebræt.explanation: "Et skærebræt" means "a cutting board": Løgene ligger på skærebrættet (The onions are on the cutting board). It is built from at skære (to cut) and bræt (board).

sentence.da: Jeg skærer tomaterne på et **skærebræt** af træ.
sentence.en: I cut the tomatoes on a wooden cutting board.

et skærmbillede.explanation: "Et skærmbillede" means "a screenshot", a picture of what is on your phone or computer: Jeg tog et skærmbillede af fejlen (I took a screenshot of the error). It is built from skærm (screen) and billede (picture).

sentence.da: Jeg tog et **skærmbillede** af beskeden.
sentence.en: I took a screenshot of the message.

et slagsmål.explanation: "Et slagsmål" means "a fight" with fists: Der var et slagsmål på gaden (There was a fight on the street). For a fight with words, use et skænderi (an argument).

sentence.da: Drengene kom i **slagsmål** efter skole.
sentence.en: The boys got into a fight after school.

et slips.explanation: "Et slips" means "a tie", the cloth you wear around your neck with a shirt: Han tager slips på (He puts on a tie). For a tied game, use uafgjort (tied).

sentence.da: Min far har **slips** på til mødet.
sentence.en: My father is wearing a tie to the meeting.

et slot.explanation: "Et slot" means "a castle" and also "a palace": Vi besøgte et gammelt slot (We visited an old castle). Danish uses the same word for both.

sentence.da: Kongen bor på et stort **slot**.
sentence.en: The king lives in a big castle.

et smil.explanation: "Et smil" means "a smile", the friendly look you make with your mouth, without any sound: Et smil kan gøre en dårlig dag bedre (A smile can make a bad day better).

sentence.da: Hun gav mig et **smil** og sagde hej.
sentence.en: She gave me a smile and said hi.

et smykke.explanation: "Et smykke" means "a piece of jewelry", one item you wear for decoration: Det er et smukt smykke (It is a beautiful piece of jewelry).

sentence.da: Hun har et smukt **smykke** om halsen.
sentence.en: She has a beautiful piece of jewelry around her neck.

et småbarn.explanation: "Et småbarn" means "a toddler", a child of about one to three years. It is built from små (small) and barn (child): Vores småbarn sover om eftermiddagen (Our toddler sleeps in the afternoon).

sentence.da: Et **småbarn** er for lille til at gå i skole.
sentence.en: A toddler is too little to go to school.

et smørrebrød.explanation: "Et smørrebrød" means "an open sandwich", rye bread with toppings and no top slice: Jeg spiser to smørrebrød (I eat two open sandwiches). It is built from smør (butter) and brød (bread).

sentence.da: Til frokost bestiller vi **smørrebrød** med fisk.
sentence.en: For lunch we order open sandwiches with fish.

et snefnug.explanation: "Et snefnug" means "a snowflake", one tiny flake of falling snow. It is built from sne (snow) and fnug (a bit of fluff).

sentence.da: Det første **snefnug** smelter i min hånd.
sentence.en: The first snowflake melts in my hand.

et sofabord.explanation: "Et sofabord" means "a coffee table". It is built from sofa (sofa) and bord (table), so it is the low table in front of the sofa.

sentence.da: Kopperne står på et lille **sofabord**.
sentence.en: The cups are on a small coffee table.

et solbær.explanation: "Et solbær" means "a blackcurrant", a small dark berry. Do not mix it up with et ribs (a redcurrant): Solbær er sorte, og ribs er røde (Blackcurrants are black, and redcurrants are red).

sentence.da: Jeg laver saft af **solbær** og vand.
sentence.en: I make juice from blackcurrants and water.

et solcenter.explanation: "Et solcenter" means "a tanning salon", where you pay to lie in a sunbed. It is built from sol (sun) and center (center): Hun går i solcenter hver uge (She goes to a tanning salon every week).

sentence.da: Hun tager i **solcenter**, fordi hun vil være brun.
sentence.en: She goes to a tanning salon because she wants to be tan.

et sommerhus.explanation: "Et sommerhus" means "a summer house" or "a cottage", a vacation home for weekends and summers. It is built from sommer (summer) and hus (house): Familien har et sommerhus ved havet (The family has a summer house by the sea).

sentence.da: Vi tager i **sommerhus** hver sommer.
sentence.en: We go to the summer house every summer.

et sommerhusområde.explanation: "Et sommerhusområde" means "a summer house area", a zone with many vacation cottages, often near the sea: Vi bor i et sommerhusområde ved vandet (We live in a summer house area by the water). It is built from sommerhus (summer house) and område (area).

sentence.da: Om vinteren er der stille i vores **sommerhusområde**.
sentence.en: In the winter, it is quiet in our summer house area.

et sommerjob.explanation: "Et sommerjob" means "a summer job", work you do during the summer vacation, often as a student: Jeg har et sommerjob i en butik (I have a summer job in a store). It is built from sommer (summer) and et job (a job).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have et **sommerjob** i en café.
sentence.en: I would like a summer job in a café.

et soundtrack.explanation: "Et soundtrack" means "a soundtrack", the music of a film, show or game: Jeg elsker filmens soundtrack (I love the film's soundtrack). Spillet har et godt soundtrack (The game has a good soundtrack).

sentence.da: Filmen har et flot **soundtrack**.
sentence.en: The movie has a nice soundtrack.

et soveværelse.explanation: "Et soveværelse" means "a bedroom". It is built from sove (to sleep) and værelse (room), so it is literally a sleeping room.

sentence.da: Jeg sover i min seng i mit **soveværelse**.
sentence.en: I sleep in my bed in my bedroom.

et spejl.explanation: "Et spejl" means "a mirror", a flat piece of glass that shows you your own face. Jeg kigger i spejlet (I look in the mirror).

sentence.da: Jeg kan se mit ansigt i et **spejl**.
sentence.en: I can see my face in a mirror.

et spejlæg.explanation: "Et spejlæg" means "a fried egg" with a whole yolk, sunny side up. It is built from et spejl (a mirror) and et æg (an egg).

sentence.da: Han steger et **spejlæg** til morgenmad.
sentence.en: He fries a sunny-side-up egg for breakfast.

et spil.explanation: "Et spil" means "a game", such as a board game, card game or computer game. It comes from at spille (to play), which is also the word for playing music.

sentence.da: Skak er et **spil** for to personer.
sentence.en: Chess is a game for two people.

et spisebord.explanation: "Et spisebord" means "a dining table". It is built from at spise (to eat) and bord (table): Vi sidder ved spisebordet (We are sitting at the dining table).

sentence.da: Vi har et stort **spisebord**, så der er plads til alle.
sentence.en: We have a big dining table, so there is room for everyone.

et spisekammer.explanation: "Et spisekammer" means "a pantry", a small room or cupboard for storing food: Der er mel i spisekammeret (There is flour in the pantry).

sentence.da: Jeg lægger pasta og ris i vores **spisekammer**.
sentence.en: I put pasta and rice in our pantry.

et spor.explanation: "Et spor" means "a track" and "a trace": Der er spor i sneen (There are tracks in the snow). At a train station, it is the platform: Toget kommer til spor 3 (The train comes to track 3).

sentence.da: Politiet fandt et **spor** efter tyven.
sentence.en: The police found a trace of the thief.

et springvand.explanation: "Et springvand" means "a fountain", water that shoots up in a square or a park: Børnene leger ved springvandet (The children play by the fountain). It is built from springe (jump) and vand (water).

sentence.da: Der er et smukt **springvand** midt i parken.
sentence.en: There is a beautiful fountain in the middle of the park.

et sprog.explanation: "Et sprog" means "a language", such as English or Spanish. People ask Taler du engelsk? (Do you speak English?) to find a language they share.

sentence.da: Dansk og engelsk er to **sprog**.
sentence.en: Danish and English are two languages.

et sprogcenter.explanation: "Et sprogcenter" means "a language center", a school where adults learn a language. It is built from et sprog (a language) and et center (a center): Hun underviser på sprogcentret (She teaches at the language center).

sentence.da: Jeg lærer dansk på et **sprogcenter** hver dag.
sentence.en: I learn Danish at a language center every day.

et spædbarn.explanation: "Et spædbarn" means "an infant", a baby in its first months: Hun passer et spædbarn (She is taking care of an infant). A more everyday word is en baby (a baby).

sentence.da: Et **spædbarn** sover det meste af dagen.
sentence.en: An infant sleeps most of the day.

et spøgelse.explanation: "Et spøgelse" means "a ghost", the spirit of a dead person: Jeg tror ikke på spøgelser (I do not believe in ghosts).

sentence.da: Der er et **spøgelse** i det gamle hus.
sentence.en: There is a ghost in the old house.

et spørgsmål.explanation: "Et spørgsmål" means "a question". A polite way to start is Må jeg stille et spørgsmål? (May I ask a question?), which literally means put a question.

sentence.da: Læreren svarer på mit **spørgsmål**.
sentence.en: The teacher answers my question.

et spørgsmålstegn.explanation: "Et spørgsmålstegn" means "a question mark", built from spørgsmål (question) and tegn (sign). It comes at the end of a question: Hvad hedder du? (What is your name?)

sentence.da: Sætningen slutter med et **spørgsmålstegn**, fordi den er et spørgsmål.
sentence.en: The sentence ends with a question mark because it is a question.

et stadion.explanation: "Et stadion" means "a stadium", where big matches and concerts are held: Der er koncert på stadion i aften (There is a concert at the stadium tonight).

sentence.da: Der er mange mennesker på **stadion** i dag.
sentence.en: There are many people at the stadium today.

et stearinlys.explanation: "Et stearinlys" means "a candle", a stick of wax that you light on the table or in the window: Jeg tænder et stearinlys (I light a candle).

sentence.da: Hun tænder et **stearinlys**, når det bliver mørkt.
sentence.en: She lights a candle when it gets dark.

et sted.explanation: "Et sted" means "a place" or "a spot", and also "somewhere": Jeg har set det et sted means "I have seen it somewhere".

sentence.da: Er der et **sted** at spise her?
sentence.en: Is there a place to eat here?

et stik.explanation: "Et stik" means "a plug" and also "a sting" or "a prick", such as from an insect or a needle. Et stik fra en bi gør ondt (A sting from a bee hurts).

sentence.da: Sæt dit **stik** i væggen, så virker lampen.
sentence.en: Put your plug in the wall and the lamp works.

et stof.explanation: "Et stof" means "a fabric", and also "a drug" or "a substance": Stoffet er blødt (The fabric is soft). Det er et farligt stof (It is a dangerous drug).

sentence.da: Jeg vil sy en kjole af dette **stof**.
sentence.en: I want to sew a dress from this fabric.

et stoppested.explanation: "Et stoppested" means "a stop". It is built from stoppe (to stop) and sted (place). For a bus, say et busstoppested (a bus stop).

sentence.da: Næste **stoppested** er banegården.
sentence.en: The next stop is the railway station.

et storindkøb.explanation: "Et storindkøb" means "a big grocery shop", buying lots of food at once: Bilen er fuld af varer efter storindkøbet (The car is full of groceries after the big shop).

sentence.da: Vi laver et **storindkøb** i supermarkedet hver lørdag.
sentence.en: We do a big grocery shop at the supermarket every Saturday.

et strygebræt.explanation: "Et strygebræt" means "an ironing board". It is built from at stryge (to iron) and et bræt (a board): Strygebrættet står i soveværelset (The ironing board is in the bedroom).

sentence.da: Hun stryger skjorten på et **strygebræt**.
sentence.en: She irons the shirt on an ironing board.

et strygejern.explanation: "Et strygejern" means "an iron" for clothes. It is built from at stryge (to iron) and jern (the metal iron): Strygejernet er varmt (The iron is hot).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **strygejern** til skjorten.
sentence.en: I use an iron on the shirt.

et strømstik.explanation: "Et strømstik" means "a power plug", the part on the end of a cord that goes into the wall: Sæt strømstikket i væggen (Put the power plug in the wall).

sentence.da: Der sidder et **strømstik** for enden af ledningen.
sentence.en: There is a power plug at the end of the cord.

et stykke.explanation: "Et stykke" means "a piece", as in et stykke kage (a piece of cake). In stores it also means "each": ti kroner stykket means "ten kroner each".

sentence.da: Må jeg få et **stykke** kage?
sentence.en: May I have a piece of cake?

et sugerør.explanation: "Et sugerør" means "a drinking straw", the thin tube you drink through: Må jeg få et sugerør til min sodavand? (May I have a straw for my soda?)

sentence.da: Hun drikker sin juice med **sugerør**.
sentence.en: She drinks her juice with a straw.

et sundhedskort.explanation: "Et sundhedskort" means "a health insurance card", the card you show at the doctor or the hospital: Husk dit sundhedskort (Remember your health card).

sentence.da: Du skal vise dit **sundhedskort** hos lægen.
sentence.en: You have to show your health insurance card at the doctor.

et supermarked.explanation: "Et supermarked" means "a supermarket". It is built from super (super) and marked (market). You can ask Hvor er supermarkedet? (Where is the supermarket?).

sentence.da: Et **supermarked** sælger mad og mange andre ting.
sentence.en: A supermarket sells food and many other things.

et svar.explanation: "Et svar" means "an answer" or "a reply", what you give to a question or a message. Tak for svaret means "thanks for the reply".

sentence.da: Hun giver et **svar** på spørgsmålet.
sentence.en: She gives an answer to the question.

et svin.explanation: "Et svin" means "a pig". Calling a person et svin is rude: Han er et svin means "He is a pig". For the meat, Danes say svinekød (pork).

sentence.da: Bonden har et **svin** på gården.
sentence.en: The farmer has a pig on the farm.

et sving.explanation: "Et sving" means "a turn" or "a curve", for example in a road: Der er et skarpt sving her (There is a sharp curve here). Bilen tog svinget (The car took the turn).

sentence.da: Pas på, der er et skarpt **sving** forude.
sentence.en: Be careful, there is a sharp curve ahead.

et sygehus.explanation: "Et sygehus" means "a hospital". It is built from syg (sick) and hus (house). Et hospital (a hospital) means the same. Hun er på sygehuset (She is at the hospital).

sentence.da: Lægen og sygeplejerskerne arbejder på et **sygehus**.
sentence.en: The doctor and the nurses work at a hospital.

et symbol.explanation: "Et symbol" means "a symbol", a sign that stands for an idea: Duen er et symbol på fred (The dove is a symbol of peace).

sentence.da: Hjertet er et **symbol** på kærlighed.
sentence.en: The heart is a symbol of love.

et syn.explanation: "Et syn" means "a sight" and also "vision", your ability to see: Det var et smukt syn (It was a beautiful sight). Hun har godt syn (She has good eyesight).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar har dårligt **syn** og bruger briller.
sentence.en: My grandfather has bad eyesight and wears glasses.

et system.explanation: "Et system" means "a system", a set of parts or rules that work together: Skolen har et nyt system til lektier (The school has a new system for homework).

sentence.da: Et **system** hjælper os med at holde orden.
sentence.en: A system helps us keep things in order.

et sår.explanation: "Et sår" means "a wound" or "a sore", such as a cut or a scrape. Et sår i munden means "a sore in the mouth".

sentence.da: Jeg har et **sår** på mit knæ.
sentence.en: I have a wound on my knee.

et sæde.explanation: "Et sæde" means "a seat" in a car, plane or train: Mit sæde er ved vinduet (My seat is by the window). A chair is en stol, not et sæde.

sentence.da: Barnet sidder i et **sæde** bag i bilen.
sentence.en: The child sits in a seat in the back of the car.

et søm.explanation: "Et søm" means "a nail": Han slår et søm i væggen (He hits a nail into the wall). Do not mix it up with en skrue (a screw), which you turn in.

sentence.da: Jeg hænger billedet op med et **søm**.
sentence.en: I hang the picture up with a nail.

saft.explanation: "Saft" means "cordial" or "squash", a sweet fruit syrup that you mix with water. It is not the same as en juice (a juice): Jeg blander saft med koldt vand (I mix cordial with cold water).

sentence.da: **Saft** laves af frugt og er meget sød.
sentence.en: Cordial is made from fruit and is very sweet.

saftevand.explanation: "Saftevand" means "diluted cordial", fruit syrup mixed with water. Børnene drikker saftevand til frokost (The children drink diluted cordial at lunch). Saft (cordial) is the syrup before you add the water.

sentence.da: **Saftevand** er saft blandet med vand.
sentence.en: Diluted cordial is cordial mixed with water.

salt.explanation: "Salt" means "salt". You do not count it, so you say noget salt (some salt) rather than a salt. The same word also describes taste: det er for salt means "it is too salty".

sentence.da: Der er meget **salt** i havet.
sentence.en: There is a lot of salt in the sea.

saltet.explanation: "Saltet" means "salted" and comes from at salte (to salt). Do not mix it up with salt, which describes taste and means "salty".

sentence.da: Fisken er **saltet** og smager af salt.
sentence.en: The fish is salted and tastes of salt.

samme.explanation: "Samme" means "same". It usually follows den, det or de (all three mean "the"), but it can also stand alone, as in samme dag (the same day). Det samme is also a reply meaning "the same to you".

sentence.da: Vi har den **samme** bil.
sentence.en: We have the same car.

sammen.explanation: "Sammen" means "together". Compare Vi spiser sammen (We eat together) with Jeg spiser alene (I eat alone). Alle sammen means "everyone together", as in Hej alle sammen! (Hello everyone!).

sentence.da: Min ven og jeg bor **sammen**.
sentence.en: My friend and I live together.

samtidig.explanation: "Samtidig" means "simultaneously", or "at the same time": Vi gik samtidig (We left at the same time). Add med to say with what: samtidig med mødet (at the same time as the meeting).

forms.en: They arrived at the same time.
She laughed and cried at the same time.
At the same time, it is cheap.

sentence.da: Han taler og spiser **samtidig**.
sentence.en: He talks and eats at the same time.

sand.explanation: "Sand" means "sand": Der er sand i mine sko (There is sand in my shoes). Do not mix it up with sand meaning "true", as in Det er sandt (That is true).

sentence.da: På stranden er der meget **sand**.
sentence.en: There is a lot of sand on the beach.

sandaler.explanation: "Sandaler" means "sandals", open shoes with straps that you wear in warm weather. One sandal is en sandal, but shoes come in pairs, so you mostly hear sandaler.

sentence.da: Om sommeren går jeg i **sandaler**.
sentence.en: In summer I wear sandals.

sandsynlig.explanation: "Sandsynlig" means "likely" or "probable" and says that something will probably happen. It is more certain than just possible. Det er sandsynligt, at han kommer (It is likely that he is coming).

sentence.da: Regn er **sandsynlig**, fordi himlen er mørk.
sentence.en: Rain is likely because the sky is dark.

sandsynligvis.explanation: "Sandsynligvis" means "probably" and is built from sandsynlig (likely): Hun kommer sandsynligvis for sent (She is probably coming too late). It is more sure than muligvis (possibly).

sentence.da: Det bliver **sandsynligvis** koldt i morgen.
sentence.en: It will probably be cold tomorrow.

sej.explanation: "Sej" means "tough" or "cool". For a person, it is a compliment: Hun er sej (She is cool). For food, it means chewy: sejt kød (tough meat).

sentence.da: Han er **sej** og giver aldrig op.
sentence.en: He is tough and never gives up.

seks.explanation: "Seks" means "six". Compare seks børn (six children) with syv børn (seven children). It is used for time too: Klokken er seks (It is six o'clock).

sentence.da: To gange tre er **seks**.
sentence.en: Two times three is six.

seksten.explanation: "Seksten" means "sixteen". Do not mix it up with seks (six): seks børn (six children), seksten børn (sixteen children). It is used for age: Jeg er seksten år (I am sixteen years old).

sentence.da: Ti plus seks er **seksten**.
sentence.en: Ten plus six is sixteen.

selleri.explanation: "Selleri" means "celery". Stangselleri (celery stalks) is the green stalk, and knoldselleri (celeriac) is the round root.

sentence.da: Jeg skærer **selleri** og gulerod til suppen.
sentence.en: I cut celery and carrot for the soup.

selv.explanation: "Selv" means "myself", yourself, herself and so on, with nobody helping: Jeg gør det selv (I do it myself). At the start of a sentence it means "even": Selv børn kan det (Even children can do it).

sentence.da: Jeg laver maden **selv**.
sentence.en: I make the food myself.

selv tak.explanation: "Selv tak" means "you're welcome". It literally means "thanks yourself", which is why it also returns thanks: Tak for i aftes - Selv tak (Thanks for last night - Thanks to you too).

forms.en: Thanks for the help. - You're welcome.

forms.da: Tak for i aftes. - Selv tak.
forms.en: Thanks for last night. - Thanks to you too.

sentence.da: "Tak for hjælpen!" - "**Selv tak**!"
sentence.en: "Thanks for the help!" - "You're welcome!"

selvfølgelig.explanation: "Selvfølgelig" means "of course". It agrees to a request, and it also says something is obvious: Hun kommer selvfølgelig for sent (Of course she is coming late).

sentence.da: "Må jeg låne din bog?" - "**Selvfølgelig**!"
sentence.en: "May I borrow your book?" - "Of course!"

selvom.explanation: "Selvom" means "even though" and introduces something you would not expect: Jeg går en tur, selvom det regner (I am going for a walk even though it is raining). After it comes a full sentence, unlike på trods af (despite), which is followed by a thing: på trods af regnen (despite the rain).

forms.en: even though he does not know

sentence.da: Jeg løber, **selvom** jeg er meget træt.
sentence.en: I am running even though I am very tired.

selvsikker.explanation: "Selvsikker" means "confident" and describes someone who believes in themselves: Hun er selvsikker, når hun taler (She is confident when she talks). It is built from selv (self) and sikker (sure).

sentence.da: Hun er **selvsikker** og taler højt foran alle.
sentence.en: She is confident and speaks loudly in front of everyone.

selvtillid.explanation: "Selvtillid" means "self-confidence", the belief that you can do things well: Hun fik mere selvtillid efter prøven (She gained more self-confidence after the test).

sentence.da: Hun har stor **selvtillid** og er aldrig bange.
sentence.en: She has great self-confidence and is never afraid.

senere.explanation: "Senere" means "later", as in Vi ses senere (See you later) and senere i dag (later today). Do not mix it up with sent, which means "late": Det er sent (It is late).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til dig **senere**.
sentence.en: I will call you later.

seneste.explanation: "Seneste" means "latest" or "most recent": Har du set hans seneste film? (Have you seen his latest movie?) It also works for a stretch of time: de seneste uger (the last few weeks). For the final one, use sidste (last).

sentence.da: Har du hørt den **seneste** nyhed?
sentence.en: Have you heard the latest news?

sengetid.explanation: "Sengetid" means "bedtime", the time to go to sleep. It is built from seng (bed) and tid (time): Børnene har sengetid klokken otte (The kids have bedtime at eight).

sentence.da: Nu er det **sengetid**, og børnene er trætte.
sentence.en: Now it is bedtime, and the kids are tired.

sennep.explanation: "Sennep" means "mustard". You do not count it, so you say noget sennep (some mustard), as in Vil du have noget sennep? (Do you want some mustard?).

sentence.da: Pølsen smager godt med ketchup og **sennep**.
sentence.en: The sausage tastes good with ketchup and mustard.

sent.explanation: "Sent" means "late", as in not early: Vi kom sent hjem (We came home late). Do not mix it up with senere, which means "later". To say you are running late, say Jeg kommer for sent (I am coming too late) or Jeg er forsinket (I am delayed).

sentence.da: Vi kommer **sent** hjem i dag.
sentence.en: We come home late today.

september.explanation: "September" means "September", the ninth month. Month names are not capitalized in Danish, unlike in English: Vi rejser i september (We travel in September).

sentence.da: Børnene starter i skole igen i **september**.
sentence.en: The children start school again in September.

seriøs.explanation: "Seriøs" means "serious" and describes someone who is earnest or a thing that is meant for real: Hun er meget seriøs (She is very serious). Er du seriøs? (Are you serious?)

sentence.da: Han er meget **seriøs** og laver aldrig sjov.
sentence.en: He is very serious and never jokes.

ses i morgen.explanation: "Ses i morgen" means "see you tomorrow". Swap i morgen for another time: ses i aften (see you tonight).

forms.en: Will we see each other tomorrow?

sentence.da: Jeg skal hjem nu. **Ses i morgen**!
sentence.en: I am going home now. See you tomorrow!

sexet.explanation: "Sexet" means "sexy", for someone or something attractive: en sexet kjole (a sexy dress). In casual talk it can also mean "cool and appealing": Det er et sexet design (That is a sexy design).

sentence.da: Hun har en **sexet** kjole på.
sentence.en: She is wearing a sexy dress.

shampoo.explanation: "Shampoo" means "shampoo" and is spelled the same as in English. You do not count it, so you say noget shampoo (some shampoo).

sentence.da: Jeg vasker mit hår med **shampoo**.
sentence.en: I wash my hair with shampoo.

shorts.explanation: "Shorts" means "shorts". It is always used for more than one: Mine shorts er nye (My shorts are new).

sentence.da: Jeg har **shorts** og T-shirt på.
sentence.en: I am wearing shorts and a T-shirt.

siden.explanation: "Siden" means "since" and also "ago". Since: siden i går (since yesterday). Ago: for to år siden (two years ago), where siden comes last.

sentence.da: Jeg har boet her **siden** 2020.
sentence.en: I have lived here since 2020.

sidst.explanation: "Sidst" means "last" in the sense of coming after everyone else or at the end: Jeg kom sidst (I came last). Before a thing, use sidste, as in sidste gang (the last time).

sentence.da: Han kom **sidst** til festen.
sentence.en: He came last to the party.

sidste.explanation: "Sidste" means "last" before a thing: den sidste bus (the last bus), sidste uge (last week), sidste år (last year). Compare Jeg kom sidst (I came last), where sidst stands alone with nothing after it.

sentence.da: Det er den **sidste** bus i dag.
sentence.en: It is the last bus today.

sig.explanation: "Sig" means "himself", "herself", "itself" or "themselves". Compare Han vasker ham (He washes him, someone else) with Han vasker sig (He washes himself). Some verbs always take sig: at skynde sig (to hurry), at glæde sig (to look forward to).

forms.en: She is looking forward to it.

sentence.da: Han vasker **sig** hver morgen.
sentence.en: He washes himself every morning.

sikke.explanation: "Sikke" means "what a ..." and starts an exclamation. It is followed by en or et to match the word: Sikke en overraskelse! (What a surprise!) and Sikke et vejr! (What weather!).

sentence.da: Åh, **sikke** en flot hund du har!
sentence.en: Oh, what a nice dog you have!

sikke en dag.explanation: "Sikke en dag" means "what a day" and reacts to a day that was great, hard or surprising. Sikke en goes with en-words. With et-words, use sikke et: Sikke et vejr! (What weather!).

forms.da: Sikke en dag, alt gik galt!
forms.en: What a day, everything went wrong!

sentence.da: **Sikke en dag**, vi vandt hele turneringen!
sentence.en: What a day, we won the whole tournament!

sikke noget.explanation: "Sikke noget" means "what a thing" or "wow", said when something surprises you: Sikke noget vejr! (What weather!). It can show amazement or annoyance, and the tone shows which.

sentence.da: **Sikke noget** rod, der er mel overalt!
sentence.en: What a mess, there is flour everywhere!

sikker.explanation: "Sikker" means "sure" and "safe". It says that someone has no doubt, or that something cannot hurt you. Er du sikker? (Are you sure?) is the usual way to check a fact.

sentence.da: Jeg er helt **sikker** på det.
sentence.en: I am completely sure about it.

sikkerhed.explanation: "Sikkerhed" means "security" and "safety": Sikkerhed er vigtig på nettet (Security is important online). It can also mean "being sure": Jeg ved det med sikkerhed (I know it for sure).

sentence.da: Bilbælter giver **sikkerhed** i trafikken.
sentence.en: Seat belts give safety in traffic.

sild.explanation: "Sild" means "herring", a small silvery fish: Jeg elsker marineret sild (I love pickled herring).

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser vi **sild** på rugbrød.
sentence.en: For lunch we eat herring on rye bread.

silke.explanation: "Silke" means "silk", a soft, shiny, light cloth used for scarves, ties and fine clothes. It is the material itself, so it takes no en or et: Jeg elsker silke (I love silk).

sentence.da: Hendes kjole er lavet af **silke**.
sentence.en: Her dress is made of silk.

simpel.explanation: "Simpel" means "simple", easy to understand or do: en simpel opskrift (a simple recipe). It can also mean plain, with nothing extra: et simpelt hus (a plain house).

sentence.da: Det er en **simpel** opgave, og børn kan klare den.
sentence.en: It is a simple task, and children can handle it.

simpelthen.explanation: "Simpelthen" means "simply" and adds force: Det er simpelthen fantastisk (It is simply fantastic). It can also mean "just": Jeg kan simpelthen ikke mere (I just can't anymore).

forms.en: I simply do not understand it

sentence.da: Det er **simpelthen** den bedste kage.
sentence.en: It is simply the best cake.

sin.explanation: "Sin" means "his own", her own or "its own" before an en-word. Compare Peter ser sin bror (Peter sees his own brother) with Peter ser Jens og hans bror (Peter sees Jens and Jens's brother). For "I" and "you" use min (my) and din (your): Jeg ser min bror (I see my brother).

sentence.da: Hun elsker **sin** hund.
sentence.en: She loves her (own) dog.

sindssyg.explanation: "Sindssyg" means "insane", and in casual talk it can also mean "wild" or "extreme": Det er sindssygt godt (It is insanely good). It is stronger than gal (crazy).

sentence.da: Det er en **sindssyg** idé, og den er farlig.
sentence.en: That is an insane idea, and it is dangerous.

sine.explanation: "Sine" means "his own" or "her own" for more than one thing. Compare Peter ser sine venner (Peter sees his own friends) with Peter ser Jens og hans venner (Peter sees Jens and Jens's friends). For one thing, use sin (en-word) or sit (et-word): sin bror (his own brother).

sentence.da: Hun ringer til **sine** forældre.
sentence.en: She calls her (own) parents.

single.explanation: "Single" means "single" in the sense of not being in a relationship: Han har været single i to år (He has been single for two years). For just one, use enkelt: en enkelt dag (a single day).

sentence.da: Jeg er **single** og har tid til venner.
sentence.en: I am single and have time for friends.

sit.explanation: "Sit" means "his own", her own or "its own" before an et-word. Compare Peter elsker sit hus (Peter loves his own house) with Peter ser Jens og hans hus (Peter sees Jens and Jens's house). For an en-word, use sin: sin bil (his own car).

sentence.da: Han passer på **sit** barn.
sentence.en: He looks after his (own) child.

sjette.explanation: "Sjette" means "sixth", as in det sjette æg (the sixth egg). It is used for dates too: den sjette maj (the sixth of May). It is not spelled sekste, even though seks (six) is the number it comes from.

sentence.da: Efter femte sal kommer **sjette** sal.
sentence.en: After the fifth floor comes the sixth floor.

sjov.explanation: "Sjov" means "fun" and also "funny": a party and a joke can both be sjov. Det var sjovt means "That was fun", and for sjov means "for fun" or "as a joke".

sentence.da: Klovnen er **sjov** og alle ler.
sentence.en: The clown is funny and everyone laughs.

sjælden.explanation: "Sjælden" means "rare", for things that are hard to find: en sjælden mønt (a rare coin). Sjældent means "rarely": Jeg ser ham sjældent (I rarely see him).

sentence.da: Det er en **sjælden** fugl i Danmark.
sentence.en: It is a rare bird in Denmark.

sjældent.explanation: "Sjældent" means "rarely": Han kommer sjældent for sent (He is rarely late). For something hard to find, use sjælden: en sjælden bog (a rare book).

sentence.da: Jeg ser **sjældent** min bror, fordi han bor langt væk.
sentence.en: I rarely see my brother because he lives far away.

skak.explanation: "Skak" means "chess" and is used without en or et: Han er god til skak (He is good at chess). In the game, Skak! (Check!) means the king is under attack, and skak mat (checkmate) ends the game.

sentence.da: Min bedstefar spiller **skak** hver søndag.
sentence.en: My grandfather plays chess every Sunday.

skal vi ikke bare...?.explanation: "Skal vi ikke bare...?" means "shall we just...?" and suggests the simple choice: Skal vi ikke bare tage hjem? (Shall we just go home?). It sounds relaxed, like an easy way out.

forms.da: Skal vi ikke bare bestille pizza?

sentence.da: **Skal vi ikke bare** tage bussen i dag?
sentence.en: Shall we just take the bus today?

skaldyr.explanation: "Skaldyr" means "shellfish". It is built from en skal (a shell) and et dyr (an animal), and it is one word for crabs, lobsters, mussels and more.

forms.en: Is there shellfish in the dish?

sentence.da: Krabber og hummere er **skaldyr**.
sentence.en: Crabs and lobsters are shellfish.

skam.explanation: "Skam" means "shame", the uncomfortable feeling after something embarrassing: Der er ingen skam i at spørge (There is no shame in asking). Det er en skam (That is a pity) uses it for something sad.

sentence.da: Hun følte **skam**, fordi alle grinede af hende.
sentence.en: She felt shame because everyone laughed at her.

skandinavien.explanation: "Skandinavien" means "Scandinavia". Place names start with a capital letter in Danish, but skandinavisk (Scandinavian) does not. To include Finland and Iceland too, Danes say Norden (the Nordic countries).

sentence.da: Danmark ligger i **Skandinavien**.
sentence.en: Denmark is in Scandinavia.

skarp.explanation: "Skarp" means "sharp" and is used for knives and edges: en skarp kniv (a sharp knife). It also describes a quick mind: Hun er meget skarp (She is very sharp).

sentence.da: Saksen er **skarp** og klipper papiret let.
sentence.en: The scissors are sharp and cut the paper easily.

skidt.explanation: "Skidt" means "bad" in casual phrases: Det gik ikke så skidt (It did not go so badly). It also means "dirt": Der er skidt på skoene (There is dirt on the shoes).

forms.en: There is dirt on the floor.

sentence.da: Maden var ikke **skidt**, men den var kold.
sentence.en: The food was not bad, but it was cold.

skiløb.explanation: "Skiløb" means "skiing", the sport: Han elsker skiløb (He loves skiing). It is built from en ski (a ski) and et løb (a run).

sentence.da: Han elsker **skiløb** og tager til Norge hver vinter.
sentence.en: He loves skiing and goes to Norway every winter.

sko.explanation: "Sko" means "shoes". It looks the same for one shoe and many: en sko (one shoe), mine sko (my shoes). Danish often says the where English says my: Jeg tager skoene på (I put my shoes on).

sentence.da: Vi har **sko** på fødderne.
sentence.en: We have shoes on our feet.

skrald.explanation: "Skrald" means "garbage", the things you throw away: Jeg tager skraldet ud (I take out the garbage). The container for it is en skraldespand (a garbage can).

sentence.da: Der ligger **skrald** på gaden.
sentence.en: There is garbage lying in the street.

skriftlig.explanation: "Skriftlig" means "written", for things done in writing rather than out loud: en skriftlig prøve (a written test). The opposite is mundtlig (oral): en mundtlig prøve (an oral test).

sentence.da: Der er både en mundtlig og en **skriftlig** prøve.
sentence.en: There is both an oral and a written test.

skræk.explanation: "Skræk" means "fright" or "terror", a sudden strong fear: Hun skreg af skræk (She screamed in terror). It is a sudden shock, not a lasting worry like bekymring (worry).

sentence.da: Han fik en **skræk**, da lyset gik ud.
sentence.en: He got a fright when the light went out.

skræmmende.explanation: "Skræmmende" means "frightening" and describes the thing that scares you: en skræmmende film (a frightening movie). To say how you feel, use bange (scared): Jeg er bange (I am scared).

sentence.da: Mørket kan være **skræmmende** for børn.
sentence.en: The dark can be frightening for children.

skræmt.explanation: "Skræmt" means "scared", frightened by something that happened: Hunden så skræmt ud (The dog looked scared). To say you fear something in general, use bange: Jeg er bange for edderkopper (I am afraid of spiders).

sentence.da: Barnet så **skræmt** ud efter tordenen.
sentence.en: The child looked scared after the thunder.

skuffet.explanation: "Skuffet" means "disappointed". Use over (about) for the cause: Jeg er skuffet over resultatet (I am disappointed with the result). Han så skuffet ud (He looked disappointed).

sentence.da: Hun var **skuffet** over sin karakter.
sentence.en: She was disappointed with her grade.

skummetmælk.explanation: "Skummetmælk" means "skim milk", milk with almost no fat. It is skummet (skimmed) and mælk (milk) joined together: Jeg køber skummetmælk (I buy skim milk).

sentence.da: **Skummetmælk** har næsten intet fedt.
sentence.en: Skim milk has almost no fat.

skyet.explanation: "Skyet" means "cloudy". It comes from en sky (a cloud). In weather forecasts, you also hear overskyet (overcast), when clouds cover the whole sky.

sentence.da: Himlen er grå og **skyet** i dag.
sentence.en: The sky is gray and cloudy today.

skyld.explanation: "Skyld" means "guilt" or "fault": Det er ikke din skyld (It is not your fault). To ask who is to blame, say Hvem har skylden? (Who is to blame?).

sentence.da: Jeg følte **skyld**, fordi jeg glemte hendes fødselsdag.
sentence.en: I felt guilt because I forgot her birthday.

skyldig.explanation: "Skyldig" means "guilty" and also "owing": Han er skyldig (He is guilty). Jeg er dig 50 kroner skyldig (I owe you 50 kroner).

sentence.da: Retten finder ham **skyldig**.
sentence.en: The court finds him guilty.

skynd dig.explanation: "Skynd dig" means "hurry up" and is said to one person. To several people, say skynd jer. The little words dig and jer mean yourself (one person) and yourselves (several people).

forms.da: Skynd dig, vi er sent på den.

sentence.da: **Skynd dig**, toget går nu!
sentence.en: Hurry up, the train is leaving now!

skål.explanation: "Skål" means "cheers". Add for and a name or dig (you) to toast someone: Skål for dig! (Cheers to you!). It is the same word as en skål (a bowl).

sentence.da: Vi løfter glassene og siger **skål**!
sentence.en: We raise the glasses and say cheers!

skøjteløb.explanation: "Skøjteløb" means "ice skating". It is built from en skøjte (an ice skate) and et løb (a run): Vi øver skøjteløb på søen (We practice ice skating on the lake).

sentence.da: Børnene elsker **skøjteløb** om vinteren.
sentence.en: The children love ice skating in the winter.

skør.explanation: "Skør" means "crazy" in a mild, playful way: en skør idé (a crazy idea). For food it means "crisp": Kiksene er skøre (The crackers are crisp).

sentence.da: Min onkel er lidt **skør**, men han er sjov.
sentence.en: My uncle is a bit crazy, but he is funny.

slet ikke.explanation: "Slet ikke" means "not at all" and makes a no stronger: Jeg er slet ikke træt (I am not tired at all). Compare Jeg er ikke træt (I am not tired).

forms.en: It is not expensive at all.
I do not understand at all.

sentence.da: Jeg er **slet ikke** sulten i dag.
sentence.en: I am not hungry at all today.
