slidt.explanation: "Slidt" means "worn": old and used up from much use, as in en slidt sofa (a worn sofa). It is also used about people: Jeg er helt slidt means "I am completely worn out".

sentence.da: Dækket er **slidt**, så vi skal have et nyt.
sentence.en: The tire is worn, so we need a new one.

slik.explanation: "Slik" means candy (sweets). You do not count it and normally use it without a: Jeg spiser for meget slik (I eat too much candy).

sentence.da: Børn elsker **slik** og kage.
sentence.en: Children love candy and cake.

slut.explanation: "Slut" means "over" or "finished", used after er (is): Ferien er slut (The holiday is over). It also means something has run out: Mælken er slut (The milk has run out).

sentence.da: Skoledagen er **slut** nu.
sentence.en: The school day is over now.

smal.explanation: "Smal" means "narrow", for streets, paths, doors and windows. It is about width, not about being thin like paper; for that use tynd (thin).

sentence.da: Den lille gade er meget **smal**.
sentence.en: The little street is very narrow.

smart.explanation: "Smart" means "smart" in the sense of clever or handy: en smart løsning (a clever solution). It can also mean "stylish": en smart jakke (a stylish jacket). For an intelligent person, klog (smart) fits better.

sentence.da: Det er en **smart** måde at spare tid på.
sentence.en: It is a clever way to save time.

smuk.explanation: "Smuk" means "beautiful", for people, places, views and things. It is a bit stronger than pæn (nice-looking). Hvor er det smukt! means "How beautiful it is!"

sentence.da: Hun har en **smuk** kjole på.
sentence.en: She is wearing a beautiful dress.

småpenge.explanation: "Småpenge" means "small change", coins of little value, and it only exists in the plural: Har du nogle småpenge? (Do you have some small change?) Det er småpenge (It is peanuts) also means a small price.

sentence.da: Har du nogle **småpenge** til automaten?
sentence.en: Do you have some small change for the machine?

småting.explanation: "Småting" means "small things" or "trifles", and it is always plural: Hun har pakket nogle småting (She has packed a few small things). It is built from små (small) and ting (things).

forms.en: I am buying some small things.

sentence.da: Jeg skal bare købe nogle **småting** i byen.
sentence.en: I just have to buy a few small things in town.

smør.explanation: "Smør" means "butter". The word for spreading it is at smøre (to spread), which looks almost the same. Smørrebrød is literally butter-bread, a slice of bread with toppings.

sentence.da: Vil du have **smør** på dit brød?
sentence.en: Do you want butter on your bread?

smøreost.explanation: "Smøreost" means "spreadable cheese", a soft cheese for bread. It is smøre (to spread) and ost (cheese) joined together: Børnene elsker smøreost på brød (The kids love spreadable cheese on bread).

sentence.da: Jeg smører **smøreost** på mit rugbrød.
sentence.en: I spread spreadable cheese on my rye bread.

snart.explanation: "Snart" means "soon": Vi ses snart (See you soon). With a clock time it means "almost": Klokken er snart ti (It is almost ten o'clock). Så snart means "as soon as".

sentence.da: Maden er **snart** klar.
sentence.en: The food will be ready soon.

snavs.explanation: "Snavs" means "dirt", the dirty stuff on clothes, floors and hands: Der er snavs på gulvet (There is dirt on the floor). It is not soil; that is jord (soil).

sentence.da: Der er meget **snavs** på mine sko.
sentence.en: There is a lot of dirt on my shoes.

snavset.explanation: "Snavset" means "dirty", covered with snavs (dirt) and in need of a wash. It is used for clothes, glasses and shoes.

sentence.da: Tøjet er **snavset** og skal vaskes.
sentence.en: The clothes are dirty and need washing.

sne.explanation: "Sne" means "snow". To say that it is snowing, use Det sner (It is snowing). It is also part of words like en snemand (a snowman) and en snebold (a snowball).

sentence.da: Børnene laver en snemand af **sne**.
sentence.en: The children make a snowman out of snow.

snue.explanation: "Snue" means "a head cold", the runny-nose kind: Han har snue (He has a head cold). Say it with no en in front. For the flu, say influenza (flu).

sentence.da: Jeg har **snue**, og min næse løber.
sentence.en: I have a head cold, and my nose is running.

social.explanation: "Social" means "social", about people who like company or things done with others: Sociale medier (social media) is a common phrase. Han er meget social (He is very social).

sentence.da: Min søster er meget **social** og elsker fester.
sentence.en: My sister is very social and loves parties.

sociale medier.explanation: "Sociale medier" means "social media" and is normally used in the plural: Sociale medier er populære (Social media are popular). Jeg har ikke tid til sociale medier (I do not have time for social media).

sentence.da: Facebook og Instagram er **sociale medier**.
sentence.en: Facebook and Instagram are social media.

software.explanation: "Software" means "software", the instructions that make a computer or phone work. The physical parts are called hardware (hardware), and Danish uses both English words as they are.

sentence.da: Vi bruger gratis **software** til at redigere billeder.
sentence.en: We use free software to edit pictures.

sojamælk.explanation: "Sojamælk" means "soy milk", a plant drink made from soybeans. It is soja (soy) and mælk (milk) joined together: Jeg bruger sojamælk i kaffen (I use soy milk in my coffee).

sentence.da: Hun drikker **sojamælk**, fordi hun er veganer.
sentence.en: She drinks soy milk because she is vegan.

sokker.explanation: "Sokker" means "socks". Danish often joins two words into one, so wool socks are uldsokker, from uld (wool) and "sokker".

sentence.da: Jeg tager **sokker** og sko på.
sentence.en: I put on socks and shoes.

solbriller.explanation: "Solbriller" means "sunglasses", from sol (sun) and briller (glasses). It is always used for more than one, even for a single pair. Briller on its own means glasses you see with.

sentence.da: Jeg tager **solbriller** på i solen.
sentence.en: I put on sunglasses in the sun.

solcreme.explanation: "Solcreme" means "sunscreen", from sol (sun) and creme (cream). When you talk about it in general, you leave out en: Husk solcreme! (Remember sunscreen!).

sentence.da: Husk at tage **solcreme** med på stranden.
sentence.en: Remember to bring sunscreen to the beach.

solid.explanation: "Solid" means "solid" and "sturdy": Bordet er solidt (The table is sturdy). It can also mean "reliable": en solid mand (a reliable man).

sentence.da: Vi byggede en **solid** hytte af sten.
sentence.en: We built a solid cabin made of stone.

solrig.explanation: "Solrig" means "sunny". When you just say what the weather is like, use solrigt: Det er solrigt i dag (It is sunny today).

sentence.da: Det er en varm og **solrig** dag.
sentence.en: It is a warm and sunny day.

solrigt.explanation: "Solrigt" means "sunny". You use it with vejr (weather), as in solrigt vejr (sunny weather), and after det er, as in Det er solrigt (It is sunny).

sentence.da: I dag er det **solrigt** og varmt.
sentence.en: Today it is sunny and warm.

solskin.explanation: "Solskin" means "sunshine", made of sol (sun) and skin (shine). The verb is at skinne (to shine): Solen skinner (The sun is shining).

sentence.da: Efter regnen kommer **solskin**.
sentence.en: After the rain comes sunshine.

solskinsvejr.explanation: "Solskinsvejr" means "sunny weather", from solskin (sunshine) and vejr (weather). It describes a clear sky and bright sun, often when planning outdoor things: Hvis det er solskinsvejr, tager vi på stranden (If it is sunny, we go to the beach).

sentence.da: Det er dejligt at gå tur i **solskinsvejr**.
sentence.en: It is lovely to go for a walk in sunny weather.

som.explanation: "Som" means "who", "that" or "which" when it joins two parts of a sentence: manden, som bor her (the man who lives here), bogen, som jeg læser (the book that I read). It also means "like" or "as": Han er som sin far (He is like his father), Jeg arbejder som lærer (I work as a teacher).

sentence.da: Det er den bog, **som** jeg læser.
sentence.en: That is the book that I am reading.

som helst.explanation: "Som helst" means "any" or "whatever" and is added to a question word: hvad som helst (anything), hvem som helst (anyone). After ikke (not), it means "at all": ikke noget som helst (nothing at all).

forms.da: Det kan være hvad som helst

sentence.da: Du kan spørge mig om hvad **som helst**.
sentence.en: You can ask me about anything.

som om.explanation: "Som om" means "as if" and compares with something that is not true or not sure: Han opfører sig, som om han ejer stedet (He acts as if he owns the place). Det ser ud, som om det regner (It looks as if it is raining).

forms.en: as if we know each other

sentence.da: Det føles **som om** vi har kendt hinanden længe.
sentence.en: It feels as if we have known each other for a long time.

som regel.explanation: "Som regel" means "as a rule", or "usually", and says what normally happens: Om søndagen sover vi som regel længe (On Sundays we usually sleep in).

forms.da: Jeg står som regel op klokken syv.
forms.en: I usually get up at seven o'clock.
As a rule we eat late.

sentence.da: Jeg drikker **som regel** kaffe om morgenen.
sentence.en: I usually drink coffee in the morning.

somme tider.explanation: "Somme tider" means "sometimes", for things that happen now and then, not every day: Somme tider tager jeg bussen (Sometimes I take the bus).

sentence.da: Jeg er **somme tider** træt om morgenen.
sentence.en: I am sometimes tired in the morning.

sommertid.explanation: "Sommertid" means "daylight saving time", when the clocks go forward one hour: Med sommertid er det lyst om aftenen (With daylight saving time it is light in the evening). In the fall, the clocks go back again.

forms.en: We switch to daylight saving time
Daylight saving time starts in March
It is daylight saving time now

sentence.da: Vi skifter til **sommertid** i marts.
sentence.en: We switch to daylight saving time in March.

sommetider.explanation: "Sommetider" means "sometimes", for things that happen now and then, not every day: Sommetider spiser vi ude (Sometimes we eat out).

forms.en: I sometimes go for a walk

sentence.da: Jeg tager **sommetider** cyklen på arbejde.
sentence.en: Sometimes I take the bike to work.

sorg.explanation: "Sorg" means "sorrow" and "grief", the deep sadness after losing someone: Han er i sorg efter sin far (He is in mourning for his father). For ordinary sadness, say Jeg er ked af det (I am sad).

sentence.da: Hele byen delte familiens **sorg**.
sentence.en: The whole town shared the family's grief.

sort.explanation: "Sort" means "black", the darkest color, the opposite of white. It is also used for coffee with no milk: sort kaffe (black coffee).

sentence.da: Natten er mørk og **sort**.
sentence.en: The night is dark and black.

sov godt.explanation: "Sov godt" means "sleep well". Sov comes from at sove (to sleep) and godt means "well".

sentence.da: Godnat, **sov godt**!
sentence.en: Good night, sleep well!

spaghetti.explanation: "Spaghetti" means "spaghetti", spelled the same as in English. You do not count it: en tallerken spaghetti (a plate of spaghetti).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **spaghetti** med kødsovs.
sentence.en: We eat spaghetti with meat sauce.

spanien.explanation: "Spanien" means "Spain". Example: Jeg elsker Spanien (I love Spain). Countries take i for being there and til for going there, as in the forms above.

sentence.da: Vi holder ferie i **Spanien**.
sentence.en: We are on holiday in Spain.

spansk.explanation: "Spansk" means "Spanish", for things from Spain and for the language. Danish writes it with a lowercase letter. For the language: Jeg taler spansk (I speak Spanish).

sentence.da: I Spanien taler man **spansk**.
sentence.en: In Spain, people speak Spanish.

speciel.explanation: "Speciel" means "special": Det er en speciel dag (It is a special day). It can also mean "odd" in a mild way: Han er lidt speciel (He is a bit odd).

sentence.da: I dag er en **speciel** dag for os.
sentence.en: Today is a special day for us.

spinat.explanation: "Spinat" means "spinach". For spinach in general, you leave out en: Jeg elsker spinat (I love spinach). Rå spinat means "raw spinach".

sentence.da: **Spinat** er grøn og sund.
sentence.en: Spinach is green and healthy.

spontan.explanation: "Spontan" means "spontaneous" and describes something done without planning: Vi tog en spontan beslutning (We made a spontaneous decision). A person who is spontan likes sudden ideas.

sentence.da: Vi tog en **spontan** tur til stranden i går.
sentence.en: We took a spontaneous trip to the beach yesterday.

sport.explanation: "Sport" means "sport". For sport in general, you leave out en. At dyrke sport means "to do sports": Han dyrker meget sport (He does a lot of sports).

sentence.da: Fodbold og tennis er **sport**.
sentence.en: Soccer and tennis are sports.

sprød.explanation: "Sprød" means "crispy" or "crunchy", for food that breaks with a snap: Brødet er sprødt udenpå (The bread is crispy on the outside). Fresh vegetables can be sprød too.

sentence.da: Jeg kan godt lide **sprød** bacon.
sentence.en: I like crispy bacon.

spændende.explanation: "Spændende" means "exciting" or "interesting". Det lyder spændende means "That sounds exciting". Interessant (interesting) is milder and fits less thrilling things.

sentence.da: Jeg læser en **spændende** bog.
sentence.en: I am reading an exciting book.

spænding.explanation: "Spænding" means "excitement" and also "tension": Børnene taler med spænding om turen (The kids talk with excitement about the trip). Der var spænding mellem dem (There was tension between them). A film that keeps you hooked is spændende (exciting).

sentence.da: Vi ventede med **spænding** på resultatet.
sentence.en: We waited with excitement for the result.

stabil.explanation: "Stabil" means "stable" and "steady": Stolen er stabil (The chair is stable). Hans helbred er stabilt (His health is steady).

sentence.da: Den nye stige er meget **stabil**, så den er sikker.
sentence.en: The new ladder is very stable, so it is safe.

stadig.explanation: "Stadig" means "still", for something that is continuing: Jeg er stadig træt (I am still tired). Endnu (yet) is used for something that has not happened: ikke endnu means "not yet".

sentence.da: Barnet sover **stadig** klokken ti.
sentence.en: The child is still sleeping at ten o'clock.

stadigvæk.explanation: "Stadigvæk" means "still", for something that keeps going: Det regner stadigvæk (It is still raining). It means the same as stadig (still). Endnu (yet) is different: ikke endnu means "not yet".

sentence.da: Han bor **stadigvæk** hos sin mor.
sentence.en: He still lives with his mother.

stakkels.explanation: "Stakkels" means "poor" in the sense of pitiful, when you feel sorry for someone: Stakkels dig! (Poor you!). For someone with no money, use fattig (poor).

sentence.da: Den **stakkels** hund er våd og kold.
sentence.en: The poor dog is wet and cold.

stegt.explanation: "Stegt" means "fried" or "roasted", food cooked in fat or in an oven, depending on the food: stegt flæsk (fried pork) and stegt kylling (roast chicken).

sentence.da: Fisken er **stegt** i panden.
sentence.en: The fish is fried in the pan.

stilhed.explanation: "Stilhed" means "silence", when nobody speaks and there is no sound: Der var stilhed i klassen (There was silence in the class). For peace and quiet, Danes say ro: Jeg vil have ro (I want peace and quiet).

sentence.da: Efter skriget var der **stilhed** i huset.
sentence.en: After the scream there was silence in the house.

stille.explanation: "Stille" means "quiet", "silent" or "calm": Vær stille means "Be quiet". For a calm, relaxed person, rolig (calm) also fits. Do not mix it up with at stille (to put or place), as in at stille et spørgsmål (to ask a question).

sentence.da: Det er meget **stille** i huset.
sentence.en: It is very quiet in the house.

stiv.explanation: "Stiv" means "stiff" and describes something that does not bend, or a body that is sore and tight: Mine ben er stive efter turen (My legs are stiff after the trip). Paper and cardboard can be stiv too.

sentence.da: Jeg er **stiv** i nakken i dag.
sentence.en: My neck is stiff today.

stolt af.explanation: "Stolt af" means "proud of": Jeg er stolt af dig (I am proud of you). Before an action, use af at: stolt af at have klaret det (proud of having managed it).

forms.da: Jeg er stolt af min datter.
forms.en: I am proud of my daughter.

forms.da: Hun er stolt af sit hus.
forms.en: She is proud of her house.
We are proud of the team.

sentence.da: Jeg er **stolt af** min lille bror.
sentence.en: I am proud of my little brother.

stolthed.explanation: "Stolthed" means "pride", the warm feeling when you or someone close did something well: Jeg føler stolthed over min søn (I feel pride about my son). The person who feels it is stolt (proud): Jeg er stolt af dig (I am proud of you).

sentence.da: Hans mor græd af **stolthed**, fordi han vandt.
sentence.en: His mother cried with pride because he won.

stop.explanation: "Stop" means "stop". Adding lige (just) makes it softer: Stop lige! (Hold on a second!).

sentence.da: **Stop**! Der kommer en bil!
sentence.en: Stop! A car is coming!

stor.explanation: "Stor" means "big" or "large". It can also mean "grown-up": Hvor er du blevet stor! means "How big you have grown!"

sentence.da: Elefanten er meget **stor**.
sentence.en: The elephant is very big.

storbritannien.explanation: "Storbritannien" means "Great Britain". It is built from stor (big) and Britannien (Britain). Example: Vi rejser til Storbritannien (We travel to Great Britain).

sentence.da: London ligger i **Storbritannien**.
sentence.en: London is in Great Britain.

stort set.explanation: "Stort set" means "basically" and "more or less": Jeg er stort set færdig (I am basically done). It says that something is nearly true, with only a small part missing.

sentence.da: Vi er **stort set** enige om det.
sentence.en: We basically agree about it.

straks.explanation: "Straks" means "right away", and often "in just a moment". It says the thing will happen almost at once, and is common when you answer someone: Vent lidt, jeg er der straks (Wait a bit, I'll be there in a moment).

sentence.da: Sæt dig ned, maden er **straks** klar.
sentence.en: Sit down, the food will be ready in a moment.

streaming.explanation: "Streaming" means "streaming", watching or listening online without saving the file first: Jeg bruger streaming til musik (I use streaming for music).

sentence.da: Vi bruger **streaming** i stedet for dvd'er.
sentence.en: We use streaming instead of DVDs.

streng.explanation: "Streng" means "strict" and describes people and rules that allow little freedom: en streng lærer (a strict teacher). It also fits a hard winter: en streng vinter (a harsh winter).

sentence.da: Vores lærer er **streng**, men retfærdig.
sentence.en: Our teacher is strict but fair.

stresset.explanation: "Stresset" means "stressed", feeling that there is too much to do: Jeg er stresset før eksamen (I am stressed before the exam). Det er stressende (It is stressful) describes the thing.

sentence.da: Hun er **stresset**, fordi hun har for meget arbejde.
sentence.en: She is stressed because she has too much work.

strikning.explanation: "Strikning" means "knitting", the activity itself: Strikning tager lang tid (Knitting takes a long time). For the action, use at strikke (to knit): Jeg strikker en trøje (I am knitting a sweater).

sentence.da: Min mormor elsker **strikning** og laver mange trøjer.
sentence.en: My grandmother loves knitting and makes many sweaters.

strøm.explanation: "Strøm" means "electricity", the power that runs your home, and also a "current" of water or air. Jeg betaler for strøm hver måned (I pay for electricity every month).

sentence.da: Lamper og computere bruger **strøm**.
sentence.en: Lamps and computers use electricity.

strømpebukser.explanation: "Strømpebukser" means "tights", the thin legwear worn under skirts and dresses. It is always plural: et par strømpebukser (a pair of tights). Jeg har hul i mine strømpebukser (I have a hole in my tights).

sentence.da: Hun har sorte **strømpebukser** på til kjolen.
sentence.en: She is wearing black tights with the dress.

stål.explanation: "Stål" means "steel", the hard, strong metal: Stål er hårdere end jern (Steel is harder than iron). You say stål with no en or et in front when you mean the material.

sentence.da: Broen er lavet af **stål** og er meget stærk.
sentence.en: The bridge is made of steel and is very strong.

stædig.explanation: "Stædig" means "stubborn" and describes someone who will not change their mind: Han er for stædig til at høre efter (He is too stubborn to listen). It is often said about children and animals.

sentence.da: Han er **stædig** og vil aldrig lytte til andre.
sentence.en: He is stubborn and never wants to listen to others.

stærk.explanation: "Stærk" means "strong", for people, coffee, tea, wind and feelings: stærk kaffe is strong coffee. For food it also means "hot" or "spicy".

sentence.da: Han er **stærk** og kan løfte tunge ting.
sentence.en: He is strong and can lift heavy things.

støj.explanation: "Støj" means "noise", the unwanted kind such as traffic or loud neighbors. A sound you like is lyd (sound), not støj: Der er for meget støj (There is too much noise).

sentence.da: Naboerne laver meget **støj** om natten.
sentence.en: The neighbors make a lot of noise at night.

støjende.explanation: "Støjende" means "noisy", for a person or place that makes a lot of noise: en støjende gade (a noisy street). For a loud sound itself, use høj: høj musik (loud music).

sentence.da: Vores naboer er meget **støjende** om natten.
sentence.en: Our neighbors are very noisy at night.

størst.explanation: "Størst" means "biggest" or "largest", the one that nothing else beats. Compare Hun er større (She is bigger) with Han er størst (He is the biggest).

sentence.da: Elefanten er **størst** af dyrene.
sentence.en: The elephant is the biggest of the animals.

støv.explanation: "Støv" means "dust", the fine dry kind that settles on shelves and floors: Der er meget støv på hylden (There is a lot of dust on the shelf). To clean it, use at tørre støv af (to wipe dust off).

sentence.da: Der er meget **støv** under sofaen.
sentence.en: There is a lot of dust under the sofa.

støvler.explanation: "Støvler" means "boots", sturdy footwear that covers the ankle or more, worn in wet or cold weather. A pair is et par støvler (a pair of boots).

sentence.da: Jeg tager **støvler** på i regnen.
sentence.en: I put on boots in the rain.

succesfuld.explanation: "Succesfuld" means "successful": Det var en succesfuld aften (It was a successful evening). It fits people, plans and businesses.

sentence.da: Hun er en **succesfuld** læge.
sentence.en: She is a successful doctor.

sukker.explanation: "Sukker" means "sugar", the sweet white stuff used in baking and drinks. It is also a main part of sweets and cake: Kage har meget sukker (Cake has a lot of sugar).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have **sukker** i kaffen.
sentence.en: I want sugar in my coffee.

sult.explanation: "Sult" means "hunger", mostly as a big or general problem: Der er sult i verden (There is hunger in the world). To say you are hungry, use sulten: Jeg er sulten (I am hungry), not Jeg har sult.

sentence.da: Mange mennesker i verden lider af **sult** og har ikke mad.
sentence.en: Many people in the world suffer from hunger and have no food.

sulten.explanation: "Sulten" means "hungry", the feeling that your body wants food. It describes a person or animal: Er du sulten? (Are you hungry?)

sentence.da: Jeg er meget **sulten** og vil spise.
sentence.en: I am very hungry and want to eat.

sund.explanation: "Sund" means "healthy", good for your body, like fruit, sleep and exercise. Do not mix it up with rask (well, not sick): Jeg er rask igen (I am well again).

sentence.da: Æbler og gulerødder er **sund** mad.
sentence.en: Apples and carrots are healthy food.

sundhed.explanation: "Sundhed" means "health" in a general sense, such as how healthy a lifestyle or a country is. For a person's own condition, Danes usually say helbred (health): Han har dårligt helbred (He is in poor health).

forms.en: It is good for your health.

sentence.da: Frugt og søvn er gode for din **sundhed**.
sentence.en: Fruit and sleep are good for your health.

super.explanation: "Super" means "great". It can stand alone: Super! (Great!). Before another word, it makes that word stronger: super god (really good).

sentence.da: Vi vandt kampen. Det var **super**!
sentence.en: We won the game. It was great!

sur.explanation: "Sur" means "sour" and also "grumpy": Citronen er sur (The lemon is sour) and Han er sur i dag (He is grumpy today).

sentence.da: Min bror er altid **sur** om morgenen.
sentence.en: My brother is always grumpy in the morning.

sur på.explanation: "Sur på" means "mad at": Han er sur på sin chef (He is mad at his boss). On its own, sur also means "sour": en sur citron (a sour lemon).

forms.da: Jeg er sur på min bror.
forms.en: I am mad at my brother.

sentence.da: Min mor er **sur på** mig i dag.
sentence.en: My mom is mad at me today.

svag.explanation: "Svag" means "weak" for people and things: Jeg er svag (I am weak). It also means "faint" for a light or a sound: et svagt lys (a faint light).

sentence.da: Han er stadig **svag** efter sygdommen.
sentence.en: He is still weak after the illness.

svensk.explanation: "Svensk" means "Swedish". It is also the name of the language: Jeg taler svensk (I speak Swedish).

sentence.da: Han kommer fra Sverige og er **svensk**.
sentence.en: He comes from Sweden and is Swedish.

sverige.explanation: "Sverige" means "Sweden". Do not mix it up with Schweiz (Switzerland), which is a different country.

sentence.da: **Sverige** er et land ved siden af Danmark.
sentence.en: Sweden is a country next to Denmark.

svigerforældre.explanation: "Svigerforældre" means "parents-in-law", the parents of your husband, wife or partner. For one, use en svigermor (mother-in-law) or en svigerfar (father-in-law): Vi spiser hos mine svigerforældre (We eat at my in-laws).

sentence.da: Min mands forældre er mine **svigerforældre**.
sentence.en: My husband's parents are my parents-in-law.

svimmel.explanation: "Svimmel" means "dizzy", the feeling that the room is spinning. You say Jeg er svimmel (I am dizzy) or Jeg bliver svimmel (I am getting dizzy).

sentence.da: Jeg er **svimmel** og skal sidde ned.
sentence.en: I am dizzy and need to sit down.

svinekød.explanation: "Svinekød" means "pork". It is built from svin (pig) and kød (meat), so it is literally pig meat.

sentence.da: **Svinekød** er kød fra en gris.
sentence.en: Pork is meat from a pig.

svær.explanation: "Svær" means "difficult" or "hard to do". Det er svært means "It is hard", and "Det er svært at lære dansk" means "It is hard to learn Danish".

sentence.da: Opgaven er meget **svær** for mig.
sentence.en: The task is very difficult for me.

svømning.explanation: "Svømning" means "swimming" as an activity or class. Compare Jeg kan svømme (I can swim) with Jeg har svømning (I have a swimming class).

sentence.da: Børnene har **svømning** i svømmehallen i dag.
sentence.en: The children have swim class at the pool today.

syd.explanation: "Syd" means "south". Compare Det er varmt i syd (It is warm in the south) with Det er koldt i nord (It is cold in the north). Use mod syd for the direction: Vi kører mod syd (We drive south).

sentence.da: Fuglene flyver mod **syd** om vinteren.
sentence.en: The birds fly south in the winter.

sydamerika.explanation: "Sydamerika" means "South America". It is made from syd (south) and Amerika (America).

sentence.da: Brasilien og Argentina ligger i **Sydamerika**.
sentence.en: Brazil and Argentina are in South America.

sydlig.explanation: "Sydlig" means "southern" and also "from the south": en sydlig vind (a southerly wind). Sønderborg ligger i det sydlige Danmark (Sønderborg is in southern Denmark).

sentence.da: Der kommer en **sydlig** vind i aften.
sentence.en: A southerly wind is coming tonight.

sydpå.explanation: "Sydpå" means "southward", toward the south, for movement: Fuglene flyver sydpå (The birds fly south). For a place, use syd for (south of): Odense ligger syd for Aarhus (Odense is south of Aarhus).

sentence.da: Vi kører **sydpå** i morgen.
sentence.en: We are driving south tomorrow.

syg.explanation: "Syg" means "sick" or "ill": Jeg er syg (I am sick). At melde sig syg means "to call in sick".

sentence.da: Min søn er **syg** og bliver hjemme.
sentence.en: My son is sick and stays home.

syltetøj.explanation: "Syltetøj" means "jam". Put the name of a fruit in front to say the kind: hindbærsyltetøj (raspberry jam), blommesyltetøj (plum jam).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have **syltetøj** på mit brød.
sentence.en: I want jam on my bread.

sympatisk.explanation: "Sympatisk" means "likeable" and is used for someone you like at first meeting: Han virker sympatisk (He seems likeable). It does not mean "sympathetic".

sentence.da: Din nye chef virker meget **sympatisk**.
sentence.en: Your new boss seems very likeable.

syning.explanation: "Syning" means "sewing", the activity itself: Syning kræver tålmodighed (Sewing takes patience). For the action, use at sy (to sew): Jeg syr en kjole (I am sewing a dress).

sentence.da: Min mor elsker **syning**, og hun syr mange kjoler.
sentence.en: My mother loves sewing, and she sews many dresses.

sytten.explanation: "Sytten" means "seventeen". Do not mix it up with syv (seven): syv børn (seven children), sytten børn (seventeen children). Example: Jeg er sytten år (I am seventeen years old).

sentence.da: Efter seksten kommer **sytten**.
sentence.en: After sixteen comes seventeen.

syv.explanation: "Syv" means "seven". Do not mix it up with sytten (seventeen): syv dage (seven days) but sytten dage (seventeen days).

sentence.da: Der er **syv** dage i en uge.
sentence.en: There are seven days in a week.

syvende.explanation: "Syvende" means "seventh". Compare syv æg (seven eggs) with det syvende æg (the seventh egg). It is used for dates too: den syvende juli (the seventh of July).

sentence.da: Søndag er den **syvende** dag i ugen.
sentence.en: Sunday is the seventh day of the week.

så.explanation: "Så" means "so" or "then". Compare Det regner, så vi bliver hjemme (It is raining, so we stay home) with Først spiser vi, og så går vi (First we eat, and then we go). Before a describing word, it adds strength: så stor (so big). Careful: så is also the past of at se (to see): Jeg så ham (I saw him).

sentence.da: Jeg er **så** glad i dag!
sentence.en: I am so happy today!

så længe.explanation: "Så længe" means "as long as". It is different from indtil (until): Jeg bliver, indtil du kommer (I stay until you come). On its own, it means "for now": Vent her så længe (Wait here for now).

forms.en: Stay as long as you like

sentence.da: Jeg er glad, **så længe** solen skinner.
sentence.en: I am happy as long as the sun shines.

så snart.explanation: "Så snart" means "as soon as" and names the moment when the next thing happens: Så snart han kom, gik vi (As soon as he came, we left). Jeg skriver, så snart jeg ved noget (I will write as soon as I know something).

forms.en: as soon as it is ready

sentence.da: Jeg ringer til dig, **så snart** jeg er hjemme.
sentence.en: I will call you as soon as I am home.

sådan.explanation: "Sådan" means "like that" or "this way". Compare Gør det sådan (Do it like this) with sådan en bil (a car like that). Said on its own, Sådan! means "There you go!" or "That's it!"

sentence.da: Se, jeg gør det **sådan**.
sentence.en: Look, I do it like this.

sådan er det bare.explanation: "Sådan er det bare" means "that's just how it is" and you use it for something that cannot be changed: Der er ofte kø her, men sådan er det bare (There is often a line here, but that's just how it is). The word bare (just) makes it sound calm.

related.en: that's just the way it is

sentence.da: Det regner meget her, men **sådan er det bare**.
sentence.en: It rains a lot here, but that's just how it is.

således.explanation: "Således" means "thus" and "like this". It shows how something is done: Gør det således (Do it like this). It is formal and mostly written. In speech, people say sådan (like this).

sentence.da: Du skal skrive det **således**.
sentence.en: You must write it like this.

såret.explanation: "Såret" means "wounded" or "hurt", for a body or for feelings: Soldaten er såret (The soldier is wounded). Hun følte sig såret (She felt hurt).

sentence.da: Hunden er **såret** i benet og kan ikke gå.
sentence.en: The dog is wounded in the leg and cannot walk.

sæbe.explanation: "Sæbe" means "soap". For an amount, you say noget sæbe (some soap) or et stykke sæbe (a piece of soap). Dish soap is a different word: opvaskemiddel (dishwashing liquid).

sentence.da: Jeg vasker mine hænder med **sæbe** og vand.
sentence.en: I wash my hands with soap and water.

særlig.explanation: "Særlig" means "special" or "particular": en særlig dag (a special day). With ikke, it means "not very": Det er ikke særlig dyrt (It is not very expensive).

sentence.da: I dag er en **særlig** dag for os.
sentence.en: Today is a special day for us.

sød.explanation: "Sød" means "sweet" in taste (sød kage, sweet cake) and also "sweet" or "cute" for people, animals and small children. A common phrase is Det er sødt af dig (That is sweet of you).

sentence.da: Kagen er for **sød** for mig.
sentence.en: The cake is too sweet for me.

sødmælk.explanation: "Sødmælk" means "whole milk", the milk with the most fat. Despite sød (sweet) in the name, it is not sweet: Jeg bruger sødmælk i kaffen (I use whole milk in my coffee).

sentence.da: Jeg vælger **sødmælk**, fordi den har mere fedt.
sentence.en: I choose whole milk because it has more fat.

sølv.explanation: "Sølv" means "silver", both the metal and the color. In sports, it is also the second-place medal: Hun vandt sølv (She won silver).

sentence.da: Min ring er lavet af **sølv**.
sentence.en: My ring is made of silver.

sølvpapir.explanation: "Sølvpapir" means "aluminum foil", the shiny sheet you wrap food in: Pak maden ind i sølvpapir (Wrap the food in aluminum foil). It is built from sølv (silver) and papir (paper).

sentence.da: Jeg pakker kartoflerne ind i **sølvpapir**.
sentence.en: I wrap the potatoes in aluminum foil.

søndag.explanation: "Søndag" means "Sunday". Day names are written with a lowercase letter in Danish. Say på søndag (on Sunday) for this coming Sunday and om søndagen (on Sundays) for every Sunday.

sentence.da: Efter lørdag kommer **søndag**.
sentence.en: After Saturday comes Sunday.

søskende.explanation: "Søskende" means "siblings", brothers and sisters as a group: Jeg har tre søskende (I have three siblings). For one person, say en bror (a brother) or en søster (a sister).

sentence.da: Jeg har to **søskende**, en bror og en søster.
sentence.en: I have two siblings, a brother and a sister.

søvn.explanation: "Søvn" means "sleep", the rest your body gets at night. It is the thing itself, not the act of sleeping, so you get it or lack it: Jeg fik lidt søvn i nat (I got little sleep last night).

sentence.da: Jeg er meget træt og har brug for **søvn**.
sentence.en: I am very tired and need sleep.
